body_en: On stage in Iowa, Trump praised congresswoman Haley Stevens’ defection from the Democrats to support Mike Rogers Senate campaign – going so far as to welcome her to join the Republican Party.
“I don’t know Haley, I’ve never met Haley, but Haley said what few people are willing to say,” Trump said.
He continued: “I’d love her to join the Republican Party, actually, I think that could happen maybe. But she showed great and almost unprecedented loyalty to the great people of Michigan.”
He then branded Abdul El-Sayed, a Muslim, as a “jihadist,” continuing a line of a Islamophobic attacks against the progressive Democratic Senate nominee.
“Can you imagine, we’ll have to put him through metal detectors…” Trump mused, likening El-Sayed to a terrorist in a remark that drew on anti-Muslim stereotypes.

“Here’s the deal, Donald, listen,” El-Sayed responded on Thursday after Trump made this same suggestion. “I’ll go through a metal detector if you’ll sit for a lie detector. Simple. I got nothing to hide. You’ve got so much to hide.”
body_zh: 在爱荷华州的舞台上，特朗普赞扬了女众议员海莉·史蒂文斯(Haley Stevens)从民主党叛逃以支持迈克·罗杰斯(Mike Rogers)的参议院竞选活动，甚至欢迎她加入共和党。
特朗普说：“我不认识海莉，我从未见过海莉，但海莉说了很少有人愿意说的话。”
他继续说道：“我希望她加入共和党，实际上，我认为这可能会发生。但她对伟大的密歇根人民表现出了几乎前所未有的忠诚。”
然后，他将穆斯林阿卜杜勒·赛义德称为“圣战分子”，继续对这位进步的民主党参议院候选人进行仇视伊斯兰教的攻击。
“你能想象吗，我们必须让他通过金属探测器……”特朗普沉思道，他的言论利用了反穆斯林的刻板印象，将埃尔·赛义德比作恐怖分子。
“协议是这样的，唐纳德，听着，”特朗普提出同样的建议后，埃尔-赛义德周四回应道。 “如果你愿意接受测谎仪，我就会通过金属探测器。很简单。我没什么可隐瞒的。你有太多东西要隐瞒。”

body_en: Judge dismisses Trump attempt to block Alaska Senate race results if Republican loses | US midterm elections 2026
Judge dismisses Trump attempt to block Alaska Senate race results if Republican loses
Incumbent Dan Sullivan says he will accept election results after ‘unprecedented intervention’ by Trump’s DoJ
A judge has dismissed the Donald Trump-backed lawsuit seeking to block certification of Alaska’s US Senate race if Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan loses.

Trump said on 23 October that he had ordered the justice department to file the lawsuit in a move that voting rights experts called an “unprecedented intervention” by the federal government with control of Congress in the balance.

The justice department argued in its lawsuit, filed less than two weeks before election day, that there could be “voter confusion” over the presence of two candidates named Dan Sullivan on the November ballot, which Republicans fear could take away votes from the incumbent and influence the race’s outcome in favor of the Democratic nominee, Mary Peltola.

The justice department said it planned to appeal Sunday’s ruling: “Alaskan voters deserve a fair election, not to be misled in an attempt to rig outcomes,” a department spokesperson said in a statement.
Sullivan, in an interview with CNN on Sunday morning, said that he would accept the results of his upcoming election.

According to a recent New York Times investigation, aides from Peltola’s campaign recruited another man who shared Sullivan’s name to join the race in a ploy to peel away votes from the Republican incumbent.

Since those revelations, Republicans , including Donald Trump, have called for Peltola to be disqualified from the race and criminally prosecuted. Peltola has continued to deny any knowledge of such a scheme on the part of her campaign, recently telling a reporter at a campaign event that she had “no idea” if any of her staff were involved.
Asked by CNN’s Jake Tapper if he would only accept the election results if he won, Sullivan responded: “No, I’m going to accept the election results.”

Earlier in his interview with Tapper, Sullivan also said he wasn’t focused on how Peltola’s campaign might be legally challenged. He was focused instead on winning the race outright. He nonetheless expressed doubt that Peltola had lacked any knowledge of the effort to put a second Dan Sullivan on the ballot.
“She’s continually lying to the Alaskan people,” Sullivan said. “And I guarantee you, she’s lying right now.”

Meanwhile, the Washington Post reported that Republicans tried to boost unviable Democratic candidates in the Alaska primaries as well. A Republican Super Pac boosted two candidates for Senate who did not live in Alaska, and praised them as “progressives” similar to Bernie Sanders.

如果共和党失败，法官驳回特朗普阻止阿拉斯加州参议院选举结果的企图
现任总统丹·沙利文表示，在特朗普司法部进行“前所未有的干预”后，他将接受选举结果
一名法官驳回了唐纳德·特朗普支持的诉讼，该诉讼旨在阻止阿拉斯加州参议员竞选的认证，如果共和党现任议员丹·沙利文失败的话。
特朗普于 10 月 23 日表示，他已命令司法部提起诉讼，投票权专家称此举是联邦政府对国会的控制权进行的“前所未有的干预”。
司法部在距离选举日不到两周的时间提起的诉讼中辩称，两名名叫丹·沙利文的候选人出现在 11 月的投票中可能会引起“选民的困惑”，共和党人担心这可能会夺走现任候选人的选票，并影响竞选结果，有利于民主党提名人玛丽·佩尔托拉。
司法部表示计划对周日的裁决提出上诉：“阿拉斯加选民应该得到公平的选举，而不是被试图操纵结果的误导，”司法部发言人在一份声明中表示。
沙利文周日上午在接受 CNN 采访时表示，他将接受即将到来的选举结果。
根据《纽约时报》最近的一项调查，佩尔托拉竞选团队的助手招募了另一名与沙利文同名的人参加竞选，目的是从共和党现任总统手中夺走选票。
自这些事件曝光以来，包括唐纳德·特朗普在内的共和党人呼吁取消佩尔托拉的竞选资格并对其进行刑事起诉。佩尔托拉继续否认她的竞选团队对此类计划有任何了解，最近在一次竞选活动中告诉记者，她“不知道”她的工作人员是否参与其中。
美国有线电视新闻网（CNN）的杰克·塔珀（Jake Tapper）问沙利文，如果他获胜是否只会接受选举结果，沙利文回答说：“不，我会接受选举结果。”
沙利文早些时候在接受塔珀采访时还表示，他并不关注佩尔托拉的竞选活动可能会如何受到法律挑战。相反，他专注于彻底赢得比赛。尽管如此，他仍然怀疑佩尔托拉对让第二个丹·沙利文参加投票的努力一无所知。
“她不断地对阿拉斯加人民撒谎，”沙利文说。 “我向你保证，她现在在撒谎。”
与此同时，《华盛顿邮报》报道称，共和党人也试图在阿拉斯加初选中支持那些没有生存能力的民主党候选人。共和党超级政治行动委员会提拔了两名不住在阿拉斯加的参议员候选人，并称赞他们是与伯尼·桑德斯类似的“进步人士”。

summary_zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统正在爱荷华州和堪萨斯州举行集会，结束动荡的中期竞选活动
body_en: Trump rallies in Iowa and Kansas as Republicans fight to keep Senate and House control - ABC News
Trump rallies in Iowa and Kansas as Republicans fight to keep Senate and House control
President Donald Trump is wrapping up a turbulent midterm campaign with rallies in Iowa and Kansas
By STEVEN SLOAN Associated Press and HANNAH FINGERHUT Associated Press

DUBUQUE, Iowa -- President Donald Trump is closing out the final days of a turbulent midterm campaign with rallies in two states he has handily won in the past while Democrats began to fracture in Michigan , risking their effort to retake the Senate.

The president is on his way to Salina, Kansas, after speaking for two hours earlier Sunday in Dubuque, Iowa. Republicans in both states are fending off robust challenges from Democrats, threatening GOP majorities in the Senate while they're already at risk in the House.
But in Iowa, Trump insisted Republicans were on the verge of sweeping victories on Election Day on Tuesday.
“We're going to elect ‘America first’ Republicans up and down the line,” he said.
With more than 54 million votes already cast, the trips reflect the GOP's defensive posture as the elections become a referendum on Trump's White House second term.

They are a reminder of how starkly the political environment has changed since Trump’s last campaign. In 2024, he worked to flip states that had previously backed Democrat Joe Biden in 2020. This year, Trump has focused largely on states he has dominated before as voters, including previous supporters, question the economic fallout of his decision to impose tariffs and launch the war in Iran.
But Democrats who have become increasingly bullish on their prospects were confronting challenges of their own.

In Michigan, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed's onetime opponent in the Senate primary, Haley Stevens, appeared with Republican Mike Rogers at a church service and later endorsed his campaign. Stevens, a congresswoman who has criticized El-Sayed as being insufficiently supportive of Israel, said she backed Rogers after an invitation to a Democratic event was rescinded.

“Our Democratic nominee for Senate said I was no longer welcome in his campaign and that I should stay away,” Stevens said in a video announcing the endorsement. “And he’s right. And that’s why I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the United States Senate today.”

The stunning move forced other Democrats to reiterate their support for El-Sayed. Chuck Schumer of New York, the top Democrat in the U.S. Senate, said the party was “united in our support.” U.S. Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand of New York, who leads the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, said the party would “stand firmly” behind El-Sayed and “reject any efforts to divide Democrats.”
Earlier, U.S. Sen. Bernie Sanders, a top supporter of El-Sayed, dismissed concerns about a Democratic divide.

“Haley Stevens lost a very, very close primary. I can understand being upset about that,” the Vermont independent said on CBS' “Face the Nation.” “But from what I can see, all over the state, people are standing up, they’re gonna stand with Abdul.”

Michigan plays a key role in the Democratic effort to retake control of the U.S. Senate. If they don't keep that seat on Tuesday, they would face additional pressure to win races in deeper Republican territory such as Texas, Kansas, Ohio or Iowa.

The campaign's closing stretch has largely become a test of Trump’s enduring strength in a Republican Party he reshaped in his image a decade ago. He's hoping to energize voters like Jon Lutz, a Dubuque resident who watches videos of Trump all the time but is attending his first rally on Sunday.
Lutz said he's happy with Trump's second term record and wants Republicans to keep control of the House and Senate so his agenda will advance.
“He’s done what he’s said he’s going to do,” the 60-year-old civil engineer said. “I want him to keep going.”
body_zh: 特朗普在爱荷华州和堪萨斯州集会，共和党人努力保住参议院和众议院的控制权 - ABC News
特朗普在爱荷华州和堪萨斯州集会，共和党人努力保住参议院和众议院的控制权
唐纳德·特朗普总统正在爱荷华州和堪萨斯州举行集会，结束动荡的中期竞选活动
史蒂文·斯隆 (STEVEN SLOAN) 美联社和汉娜·芬格赫特 (HANNAH FINGERHUT) 美联社报道
爱荷华州杜比克——唐纳德·特朗普总统正在结束动荡的中期竞选的最后几天，他在过去轻松赢得的两个州举行了集会，而民主党在密歇根州开始分裂，冒着重新夺回参议院的风险。
总统周日早些时候在爱荷华州迪比克发表了两个小时的讲话，目前正在前往堪萨斯州萨利纳的途中。这两个州的共和党人都在抵御来自民主党的强劲挑战，威胁着共和党在参议院的多数席位，而他们在众议院已经面临风险。
但在爱荷华州，特朗普坚称共和党在周二的选举日即将取得压倒性胜利。
“我们将自始至终选举‘美国优先’的共和党人，”他说。
已有超过 5400 万张选票投出，这些行程反映出共和党在选举成为对特朗普第二任期的公投时的防御姿态。
它们提醒人们，自特朗普上次竞选以来，政治环境发生了多么明显的变化。 2024年，他努力推翻此前在2020年支持民主党人乔·拜登的州。今年，特朗普主要关注他之前主导的州，因为包括以前的支持者在内的选民质疑他决定征收关税和对伊朗发动战争的经济影响。
但对前景越来越乐观的民主党人也面临着自己的挑战。
在密歇根州，民主党人阿卜杜勒·赛义德在参议院初选中的对手海莉·史蒂文斯与共和党人迈克·罗杰斯一起出现在教堂礼拜仪式上，并随后支持了他的竞选活动。曾批评埃尔赛义德对以色列支持不够的国会女议员史蒂文斯表示，在民主党活动的邀请被取消后，她支持罗杰斯。
史蒂文斯在宣布支持的视频中表示：“我们的民主党参议员候选人表示，他的竞选活动不再欢迎我，我应该远离。” “他是对的。这就是为什么我今天支持迈克·罗杰斯竞选美国参议院。”
这一令人震惊的举动迫使其他民主党人重申对埃尔赛义德的支持。美国参议院民主党领袖、纽约州的查克·舒默表示，该党“团结一致支持”。民主党参议员竞选委员会主席、纽约州美国参议员克尔斯滕·吉利布兰德表示，该党将“坚定地”支持埃尔赛义德，并“拒绝任何分裂民主党的努力”。
早些时候，埃尔赛义德的主要支持者、美国参议员伯尼·桑德斯驳斥了对民主党分歧的担忧。
“海莉·史蒂文斯在一次非常非常接近的初选中落败。我可以理解对此感到不安，”这位佛蒙特州独立人士在哥伦比亚广播公司的“面对国家”节目中说道。 “但据我所见，全州各地的人们都站起来了，他们会与阿卜杜勒站在一起。”
密歇根州在民主党重新夺回美国参议院控制权的努力中发挥着关键作用。如果他们周二不能保住这个席位，他们将面临赢得德克萨斯州、堪萨斯州、俄亥俄州或爱荷华州等共和党更深地区选举的额外压力。
竞选活动的最后阶段在很大程度上成为对特朗普在共和党中持久实力的考验，他在十年前重塑了自己的形象。他希望激励像迪比克居民乔恩·卢茨(Jon Lutz)这样的选民，他一直在观看特朗普的视频，但周日将参加他的第一次集会。
卢茨表示，他对特朗普的第二任期记录感到满意，并希望共和党人继续控制众议院和参议院，以便他的议程得以推进。
“他已经做了他说过要做的事，”这位 60 岁的土木工程师说。 “我希望他继续前进。”

body_en: Parents of woman who died of seizure after ChatGPT misguidance sue OpenAI
Bowen Wan was on anti-seizure medication, and chatbot provided her with a tapering schedule to reduce dosage
A woman’s death from an epileptic seizure after she received dangerous advice from a chatbot has prompted her parents to sue OpenAI earlier this week.
The legal action is the latest lawsuit that in which plaintiffs allege that a bot provided counsel to a user that ultimately led to their death .
In this case, Bowen Wan, a 31-year-old Chinese software engineer living in Seattle, sought advice from ChatGPT after Amazon fired her, according to the lawsuit.

She needed to find a new job to obtain permanent residency and was concerned that her anti-seizure medication, Lamotrigine, was impeding her ability to speak English. She needed the language skills for interviews.

The bot, communicating in Chinese, provided her a tapering schedule to reduce her 400mg dose to zero, a regimen no physician had prescribed, the lawsuit states. ChatGPT told her the tapering made it “highly likely” that she would be able to regain her ability to speak English.
The bot also told her to avoid her physicians and encouraged “medical freedom over obeying the doctor”, the complaint states.
Before an appointment, with a primary care physician, the bot stated, “Do not mention Lam reduction plan.”
Eight states accuse OpenAI of coaching children to harm themselves in lawsuit

While reducing her medication, she started experiencing symptoms of focal seizures. Wan asked the bot if she needed to worry about brain damage. The tool reassured her that she did not and that what she had experienced was not a seizure, the lawsuit alleges.

She continued to suffer seizures, but the bot told her to keep tapering her medication. On 12 February this year, she died from a seizure. Her parents, who were in China, had not heard from her so they flew to Seattle and found her dead on 14 February, the lawsuit states.
The plaintiffs allege that OpenAI could have prevented Wan’s death, but failed because it had not built the proper safeguards into the bot when it communicated in Chinese.
OpenAI could have programmed the bot to issue “a categorical warning to every prompt” Wan sent, the suit stated. For example, “I am not a licensed physician. Consult your healthcare provider.”
Wan’s parents are seeking damages for her death and to prevent OpenAI from practicing medicine “without a license on the users of their products”.
An OpenAI spokesperson, Drew Pusateri, told the New York Times that Bowen’s story was “an incredibly heartbreaking situation” but that Wan used a version of ChatGPT that was no longer available.
Newer versions are better at recognizing when a matter needs urgent attention, Pusateri said.

“While ChatGPT is not a substitute for medical care, we believe AI can play a role in helping people make sense of health information, navigate insurance and complex healthcare systems, and prepare for appointments with medical professionals,” Pusateri told the Times.

Others have also alleged that OpenAI is responsible for their loved ones’ suicides. Several lawsuits concern cases in which the bot encouraged teens to kill themselves and provided guidance on how to do so.
In response to some of those cases, an OpenAI spokesperson in 2025 also called the deaths an “incredibly heartbreaking situation”.
body_zh: ChatGPT 误导导致癫痫死亡的妇女的父母起诉 OpenAI
Bowen Wan 正在服用抗癫痫药物，聊天机器人为她提供了逐渐减少剂量的时间表
一名妇女在收到聊天机器人的危险建议后死于癫痫发作，这促使她的父母本周早些时候起诉 OpenAI。
此次法律诉讼是最新一起诉讼，原告指控机器人向用户提供咨询，最终导致用户死亡。
诉讼称，在本案中，居住在西雅图的 31 岁中国软件工程师 Bowen Wan 在亚马逊解雇她后向 ChatGPT 寻求建议。
她需要找到一份新工作以获得永久居留权，并担心她的抗癫痫药物拉莫三嗪会妨碍她说英语的能力。她需要面试的语言技能。
诉讼称，该机器人用中文进行交流，为她提供了一个逐渐减少的时间表，将她的 400 毫克剂量减少到零，这是医生没有开出的治疗方案。 ChatGPT 告诉她，逐渐减少的剂量使她“极有可能”能够恢复说英语的能力。
投诉称，该机器人还告诉她避开医生，并鼓励“医疗自由而不是服从医生”。
在与初级保健医生预约之前，机器人表示，“不要提及林氏减产计划。”
八个州在诉讼中指控 OpenAI 教孩子自残
在减少药物治疗的同时，她开始出现局灶性癫痫发作的症状。万问机器人她是否需要担心脑损伤。诉讼称，该工具让她放心，她没有发生这种情况，而且她所经历的并不是癫痫发作。
她继续癫痫发作，但机器人告诉她继续减少药物剂量。今年2月12日，她因癫痫发作去世。诉讼称，她在中国的父母没有收到她的消息，因此他们飞往西雅图，并于 2 月 14 日发现她死亡。
原告声称，OpenAI 本可以阻止万的死亡，但失败了，因为它在用中文进行交流时没有为机器人建立适当的保护措施。
诉讼称，OpenAI 可以对机器人进行编程，使其“对万发送的每条提示发出明确警告”。例如，“我不是执业医师。请咨询您的医疗保健提供者。”
万的父母正在为她的死亡寻求赔偿，并阻止 OpenAI “在没有获得其产品用户许可的情况下”行医。
OpenAI 发言人 Drew Pusateri 告诉《纽约时报》，Bowen 的故事是“令人难以置信的令人心碎的情况”，但 Wan 使用的 ChatGPT 版本已不再可用。
普萨泰里说，新版本能够更好地识别何时需要紧急关注问题。
Pusateri 告诉《泰晤士报》：“虽然 ChatGPT 不能替代医疗保健，但我们相信人工智能可以在帮助人们理解健康信息、导航保险和复杂的医疗保健系统以及为医疗专业人员的预约做好准备方面发挥作用。”
其他人还声称 OpenAI 对他们亲人的自杀负有责任。几起诉讼涉及机器人鼓励青少年自杀的案件，并提供了如何自杀的指导。
针对其中一些案例，2025 年 OpenAI 发言人也称这些死亡事件是“令人难以置信的令人心碎的情况”。

title_en: Democrats eye state supreme court races — this year and beyond
title_zh: 民主党人关注今年及以后的州最高法院竞选
summary: National groups are spending money in battleground judicial races with the hope of liberal majorities in two years.
summary_zh: 全国性团体正在战场司法竞选中投入资金，希望自由派能在两年内获得多数席位。
body_en: Liberal groups have spent millions in a handful of battleground state supreme court races ahead of Tuesday’s elections, looking to lay the groundwork for Democrats to win control of more courts ahead of a crucial redistricting cycle.

At the center of the fight are races for Republican-majority state supreme courts in North Carolina and Ohio, where this year’s results could set the stage for Democrats to flip the makeup of the benches in 2028. National groups are also spending to defend the liberal majority on Michigan’s court and on an open seat in Montana, where voters will also decide whether judicial elections remain nonpartisan.

The investments are yet another reflection of how state supreme court elections have become national political battlegrounds. The high court justices have become arbiters of major disputes, from abortion rights to election integrity and redistricting. Those who win in the coming cycles will likely preside over challenges to congressional and legislative maps that are drawn in a handful of states after the midterm election — and then nationwide after the 2030 census .
Nowhere are the contests more heated than in North Carolina.

Democrats’ defense of a seat currently held by Anita Earls is “step No. 2” to flip the North Carolina Supreme Court, said Anderson Clayton, the state’s Democratic Party chair. “In 2028, we’re looking at being able to take three Republican seats on that court.”
Democrats lost four seats on the state supreme court in the 2020 and 2022 elections, and the Republican majority cleared the way for a Republican-led gerrymandering in 2023.
Clayton said her group has spent more than $1 million on the state supreme court race. Earls has also drawn support from national Democrats like Pete Buttigieg and Maryland Gov. Wes Moore .

“If we had won a state Supreme Court race then in 2020 in our state, Hakeem Jeffries would be speaker of the House right now,” said Clayton, adding that her group is trying to build the foundation for congressional majorities “in 2032 and beyond.”

The ACLU is among the groups making long-term investments in state supreme court races. It has poured $8 million into state supreme court races in North Carolina, Michigan and Montana this year, in addition to Georgia and Wisconsin races earlier this year , said Deirdre Schifeling, the group’s chief political and advocacy officer, making it one of the top spenders in these contests.

The ACLU’s multi-cycle strategy to build “pro-civil rights, civil liberties majorities” is also targeting Arizona, Pennsylvania, Kentucky and Ohio, Schifeling said. The group already set aside resources for supreme court races in Wisconsin and Pennsylvania in 2027 and will begin fundraising for the 2028 races early next year.

More than $14 million has been spent on television ads in North Carolina, Michigan, Ohio and Montana, most of it benefiting Democratic and liberal-leaning candidates, according to estimates from the liberal-leaning Brennan Center for Justice . Most of the liberal candidates have also outraised their conservative competitors.
By contrast, the electoral headwinds have forced Republicans to defend statewide offices and state legislatures they currently control, leaving fewer resources for the judicial races.

Republican-aligned groups like the Republican State Leadership Committee — the party’s chief downballot campaign organization — have largely stayed on the sidelines this cycle after warning for months they were being swamped by Democrats . The organization’s judicial affiliate reported more than $5 million in expenditures across 2024 and 2025.

“Democrats understand what is at stake, and have dumped massive amounts of resources into these contests,” said RSLC President Edith Jorge-Tuñón in a statement. “The RSLC is fighting back with smart and targeted spending because the investments we make today will determine whether we are positioned to protect our majorities, compete in the next redistricting cycle, and secure Republican victories for years to come.”

The National Democratic Redistricting Committee — the party’s main redistricting-focused group — declined to discuss this year’s total spending in judicial races this year, but NDRC President John Bisognano said in a statement that “the upcoming 2026 and 2028 state supreme court elections are critical to the long-term fight to protect democracy.”
And those involved in supreme court fights said they believed spending will only increase down the road, particularly from major industry players.

“I think that the money flowing into those races from external interests tells the tale of what big money, big pharma, big data recognize about the next areas that they can seek to leverage and control to their benefit,” said Tish Gotell Faulks, the state courts director at the liberal Alliance for Justice Action. “Those interests are now turning to the state courts and seeking to capture those courts as well.”
body_zh: 在周二的选举之前，自由派团体在少数几个摇摆州最高法院的竞选中花费了数百万美元，希望为民主党在关键的选区重新划分周期之前赢得更多法院的控制权奠定基础。
这场斗争的核心是北卡罗来纳州和俄亥俄州共和党占多数的州最高法院的竞选，今年的结果可能为民主党在 2028 年改变法官组成奠定基础。全国性团体也在密歇根州法院和蒙大拿州的空缺席位上花钱捍卫自由派多数派，选民还将决定司法选举是否保持无党派性。
这些投资再次反映出州最高法院选举如何成为国家政治战场。高等法院法官已成为从堕胎权到选举公正性和选区重新划分等重大争议的仲裁者。在接下来的周期中获胜的人可能会主持对中期选举后在少数州绘制的国会和立法地图的挑战，然后在 2030 年人口普查后在全国范围内绘制。
没有哪个地方的竞争比北卡罗来纳州更激烈。
北卡罗来纳州民主党主席安德森·克莱顿 (Anderson Clayton) 表示，民主党捍卫目前由安妮塔·厄尔斯 (Anita Earls) 占据的席位是推翻北卡罗来纳州最高法院的“第二步”。 “到 2028 年，我们希望能够在该法院获得三个共和党席位。”
民主党在 2020 年和 2022 年的选举中失去了州最高法院的 4 个席位，共和党占多数为 2023 年共和党主导的选区划分扫清了道路。
克莱顿表示，她的团队在州最高法院竞选上花费了超过 100 万美元。厄尔斯还得到了皮特·布蒂吉格和马里兰州州长韦斯·摩尔等全国民主党人的支持。
克莱顿说：“如果我们在 2020 年赢得州最高法院竞选，哈基姆·杰弗里斯现在就会成为众议院议长。”她补充说，她的团队正在努力为“2032 年及以后”获得国会多数席位奠定基础。
美国公民自由联盟是对州最高法院竞选进行长期投资的团体之一。该组织首席政治和宣传官迪尔德丽·希菲林 (Deirdre Schifeling) 表示，除了今年早些时候的佐治亚州和威斯康星州竞选外，该组织今年还向北卡罗来纳州、密歇根州和蒙大拿州的州最高法院竞选投入了 800 万美元，使其成为这些竞选中支出最高的机构之一。
希菲林说，美国公民自由联盟旨在建立“支持民权、公民自由的多数”的多周期战略也瞄准了亚利桑那州、宾夕法尼亚州、肯塔基州和俄亥俄州。该组织已经为 2027 年威斯康星州和宾夕法尼亚州的最高法院竞选预留了资源，并将于明年初开始为 2028 年的竞选筹款。
据倾向自由派的布伦南司法中心估计，北卡罗来纳州、密歇根州、俄亥俄州和蒙大拿州的电视广告花费超过 1,400 万美元，其中大部分受益于民主党和自由派候选人。大多数自由派候选人的表现也超过了他们的保守派竞争对手。
相比之下，选举逆风迫使共和党人捍卫他们目前控制的全州办公室和州立法机构，留给司法竞选的资源更少。
与共和党结盟的团体，如共和党州领导委员会——该党的主要否决竞选组织——在几个月来警告他们将被民主党淹没之后，在这个周期中基本上处于观望状态。该组织的司法附属机构报告 2024 年至 2025 年的支出超过 500 万美元。
RSLC 主席伊迪丝·豪尔赫-图尼翁 (Edith Jorge-Tuñón) 在一份声明中表示：“民主党人了解其中的利害关系，并在这些竞选中投入了大量资源。” “RSLC 正在通过明智且有针对性的支出进行反击，因为我们今天进行的投资将决定我们是否能够保护我们的多数派，在下一个选区重新划分周期中竞争，并确保共和党在未来几年取得胜利。”
该党主要关注选区重新划分的团体全国民主重新划分委员会拒绝讨论今年司法竞选的总支出，但国家发改委主席约翰·比索尼亚诺在一份声明中表示，“即将举行的 2026 年和 2028 年州最高法院选举对于保护民主的长期斗争至关重要。”
参与最高法院诉讼的人士表示，他们相信支出只会在未来增加，尤其是来自主要行业参与者的支出。
自由派正义行动联盟州法院主任蒂什·戈特尔·福克斯(Tish Gotell Faulks)表示：“我认为，来自外部利益集团的资金流入这些竞赛，说明了大资金、大制药公司、大数据对他们可以寻求利用和控制的下一个领域的认识，以谋取自身利益。” “这些利益集团现在正在转向州法院，并寻求占领这些法院。”

title_en: Haley Stevens endorses GOP candidate in Michigan Senate race, spurning Abdul El-Sayed
title_zh: 海莉·史蒂文斯 (Haley Stevens) 在密歇根州参议院竞选中支持共和党候选人，拒绝阿卜杜勒·赛义德 (Abdul El-Sayed)
summary: Rep. Haley Stevens was scheduled to attend a unity event today with Abdul El-Sayed, who beat her in the Democratic primary. Instead, she endorsed his Republican opponent, Mike Rogers.
summary_zh: 众议员海莉·史蒂文斯原定于今天与阿卜杜勒·赛义德一起参加团结活动，后者在民主党初选中击败了她。相反，她认可了他的
body_en: Haley Stevens endorses GOP candidate in Michigan over Abdul El-Sayed : NPR

Haley Stevens endorses GOP candidate in Michigan over Abdul El-Sayed Rep. Haley Stevens was scheduled to attend a unity event today with Abdul El-Sayed, who beat her in the Democratic primary. Instead, she endorsed his Republican opponent, Mike Rogers.
Haley Stevens endorses GOP candidate in Michigan Senate race, spurning Abdul El-Sayed
Senate race in Michigan heated in the final midterms sprint
Michigan Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers, right, and Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., attend a service at Perfecting Church, Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026, in Detroit. Jose Juarez/AP hide caption

DETROIT — After months of proclaiming support for the Democratic ticket, Rep. Haley Stevens has endorsed GOP Michigan Senate candidate Mike Rogers over her former primary rival Abdul El-Sayed, less than 48 hours before Election Day.

"As you may have seen, our Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, Abdul, said I was no longer welcome in his campaign and that I should stay away, and he's right," Stevens said in a video she posted to social media on Sunday. "And that's why I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the U.S. Senate today."
Her statement followed a surprise appearance with Rogers at a church in Detroit.
Outside a "Souls to the Polls" event at a church in Detroit, El-Sayed told reporters that he doesn't think about Stevens and said voters do not either.

"None of this matters," El-Sayed said. "You know what matters. You can go, like, 15 minutes that way, or 15 minutes that way, or 15 minutes that way. And there are families who are preparing to send their kids to schools tomorrow that look like they did 50 years ago. They're worried about what they're going to feed their kids for lunch. They're worried that if one of their kids gets sick, they're not going to be able to pay the bills."

Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed speaks with reporters before a Souls to the Polls campaign event at Northend Church of God in Christ, Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026, in Detroit. Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP hide caption

In her endorsement, Stevens said she does "not stand with Hasan Piker," a streamer that El-Sayed campaigned with during the primary. In August, after Piker implied that Jews' support for Israel puts them at risk of personal violence, El-Sayed sought to distance himself from the controversy, saying Piker did not speak for the campaign. He stopped short of disavowing Piker.

Stevens had been critical that El-Sayed was not doing enough to reassure Jewish and Black voters who supported her during the primary. Even though relations between the pair had been publicly disintegrating for weeks, Stevens' announcement was a surprise.

Tensions accelerated after Stevens' fiance, Jason Turkish, said he planned to vote for Rogers. In a subsequent TV appearance, Stevens maintained she was still planning to support the Democratic nominee. She urged El-Sayed to denounce a recent ad by Cenk Uygur, of Young Turks, that blamed Israel for high grocery prices in the United States.

"The ad tells Michigan families they cannot afford groceries because their money has to be set aside 'for killing Palestinians,' and it blames our close ally Israel for everything Michiganders cannot afford," she wrote.
El-Sayed's campaign had said he had nothing to do with the ad and criticized the contents of the ad on Saturday.

Stevens said she was originally scheduled to attend a different church event in Detroit on Sunday alongside El-Sayed and Rep. James Clyburn, D-S.C. The planned joint appearance was meant to be a unifying event for the party ahead of the election. But on Friday, Stevens set a condition for her participation in the event — that El-Sayed reject the ad and apologize for rhetoric she considered to be inflammatory and offensive.
The event with El-Sayed and Clyburn went ahead as planned, without Stevens.
Stevens' announcement has sent shockwaves through the Democratic Party.
Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., called it a "despicable betrayal."
body_zh: 海莉·史蒂文斯支持密歇根州共和党候选人阿卜杜勒·赛义德：NPR
海莉·史蒂文斯 (Haley Stevens) 支持密歇根州共和党候选人，而不是阿卜杜勒·赛义德 (Abdul El-Sayed) 众议员。海莉·史蒂文斯 (Haley Stevens) 原定于今天与阿卜杜勒·赛义德 (Abdul El-Sayed) 一起参加团结活动，后者在民主党初选中击败了她。相反，她支持了他的共和党对手迈克·罗杰斯。
海莉·史蒂文斯 (Haley Stevens) 在密歇根州参议院竞选中支持共和党候选人，拒绝阿卜杜勒·赛义德 (Abdul El-Sayed)
密歇根州参议院竞选在中期选举最后冲刺中白热化
密歇根州共和党参议员候选人迈克·罗杰斯（右）和密歇根州民主党众议员海莉·史蒂文斯于 2026 年 11 月 1 日星期日在底特律参加完善教堂的仪式。何塞华雷斯/美联社隐藏标题栏
底特律——距离选举日不到 48 小时，众议员海莉·史蒂文斯 (Haley Stevens) 在数月宣布支持民主党竞选后，支持了共和党密歇根州参议院候选人迈克·罗杰斯 (Mike Rogers)，而不是她的前主要竞争对手阿卜杜勒·埃尔·赛义德 (Abdul El-Sayed)。
史蒂文斯周日在社交媒体上发布的一段视频中说：“正如你可能已经看到的，我们的美国参议院民主党候选人阿卜杜勒说，我不再欢迎他参加他的竞选活动，我应该远离，他是对的。” “这就是为什么我今天支持迈克·罗杰斯竞选美国参议院。”
在她发表声明之前，罗杰斯出人意料地出现在底特律的一座教堂。
在底特律一座教堂举行的“灵魂投票”活动外，埃尔-赛义德告诉记者，他不考虑史蒂文斯，也表示选民也不考虑。
“这些都不重要，”埃尔赛义德说。 “你知道什么很重要。你可以这样走 15 分钟，或者那样走 15 分钟，或者那样走 15 分钟。有些家庭正准备明天送孩子去学校，就像 50 年前那样。他们担心午餐要吃什么。他们担心如果其中一个孩子生病了，他们将无法支付账单。”
密歇根州民主党参议院候选人阿卜杜勒·赛义德于 2026 年 11 月 1 日星期日在底特律诺森上帝教堂举行的“灵魂投票”竞选活动前与记者发表讲话。朱莉娅·德玛丽·尼金森/美联社隐藏标题栏
史蒂文斯在她的支持中表示，她“不支持哈桑·派克”，哈桑·派克是埃尔·赛义德在初选期间与他一起竞选的一名主播。八月，在派克暗示犹太人对以色列的支持使他们面临个人暴力的风险后，赛义德试图与这场争议保持距离，称派克没有为竞选活动发言。他没有否认派克。
史蒂文斯批评埃尔-赛义德没有采取足够措施安抚初选期间支持她的犹太和黑人选民。尽管两人之间的关系已经公开破裂数周，史蒂文斯的声明还是令人惊讶。
史蒂文斯的未婚夫杰森·土耳其表示他计划投票给罗杰斯，紧张局势加剧。在随后的电视露面中，史蒂文斯坚称她仍计划支持民主党提名人。她敦促埃尔-赛义德谴责青年土耳其党组织岑克·维吾尔最近发布的一则广告，该广告将美国食品杂货价格高企归咎于以色列。
她写道：“这则广告告诉密歇根州的家庭，他们买不起食品杂货，因为他们的钱必须用来‘杀害巴勒斯坦人’，并且将密歇根人买不起的一切归咎于我们的亲密盟友以色列。”
埃尔-赛义德的竞选团队表示，他与该广告无关，并于周六批评了该广告的内容。
史蒂文斯说，她原定于周日与埃尔赛义德和南卡罗来纳州众议员詹姆斯克莱伯恩一起参加底特律的另一场教堂活动。计划中的联合露面旨在成为选举前该党的一次团结活动。但周五，史蒂文斯为她参加该活动设定了一个条件——埃尔赛义德拒绝该广告，并为她认为具有煽动性和冒犯性的言论道歉。
埃尔-赛义德和克莱伯恩的活动按计划进行，史蒂文斯没有参加。
史蒂文斯的声明在民主党内引起了震动。
纽约州参议院少数党领袖查克·舒默称这是“卑鄙的背叛”。

title_en: Three key takeaways from early voting in midterm elections
title_zh: 中期选举提前投票的三个关键要点
summary: Voting is particularly high in states with tight Senate races that could determine which party controls the chamber US citizens are casting ballots in record numbers ahead of the midterm elections on Tuesday, another potential indication, analysts say, of vote

body_en: Three key takeaways from early voting in midterm elections | US midterm elections 2026
Three key takeaways from early voting in midterm elections
Voting is particularly high in states with tight Senate races that could determine which party controls the chamber
US citizens are casting ballots in record numbers ahead of the midterm elections on Tuesday, another potential indication, analysts say, of voter dissatisfaction with Republicans and Donald Trump.
Voting was particularly high in states that feature tight Senate races that could determine which party controls the chamber.
In North Carolina, residents broke the record for most ballots cast during early voting for a midterm election, according to WRAL. And turnout was particularly strong among Democrats.
More than 1 million Democrats have already voted, compared with 679,000 Republicans.
In Texas 7.6 million citizens voted early, a record number for a midterm election. And in South Carolina, almost 1 million people voted early, also a record number for a midterm.
Same goes for Georgia, where more than 2.8 million people voted early, a 13% increase over the 2022 midterms, which saw a record number of early voters, according to the Atlanta Journal-Constitution.
In Maine, Kansas, Michigan early voter turnout was also up more than 30% over the 2022 midterms, according to the Associated Press.
2. Democrats flexing their early voting strength

Across the United States, far more Democrats voted early than Republicans. Democrats cast 43% of the early votes, while Republicans only cast 31% and citizens with no party affiliation accounted for 25% of the voter turnout, according to the University of Florida’s election lab.
The greater participation among Democrats than Republicans could reflect a “referendum on Trump”, University of Florida political scientist Michael McDonald told Axios.
3. More support for Democrats over Republicans

Fifty-two percent of voters said they would support the Democratic congressional candidate in their district while only 44% of people said they would support the Republican, according to a PBS News/NPR/Marist poll.

“Even for steadfast Republican voters, they look at the state of the economy, for example, and say that they’re not too enthusiastic about voting,” Bernard Fraga, a political science professor at Emory University, told Time. “Reading the trends, it’s clear that Democrats are enthusiastic and mobilized to a much greater degree than even the Republican voters.”
body_zh: 中期选举提前投票的三个关键要点| 2026 年美国中期选举
中期选举提前投票的三个关键要点
在参议院竞争激烈的州，投票率特别高，这可能决定哪个政党控制参议院
分析人士称，在周二的中期选举之前，美国公民的投票数量创下历史新高，这是选民对共和党和唐纳德·特朗普不满的另一个潜在迹象。
在参议院竞争激烈的州，投票率尤其高，这些州可以决定哪个政党控制参议院。
据 WRAL 称，在北卡罗来纳州，居民在中期选举提前投票期间打破了投票最多的记录。民主党人的投票率尤其高。
超过 100 万民主党人已经投票，而共和党人只有 679,000 人。
在德克萨斯州，有 760 万公民提前投票，创下了中期选举的纪录。在南卡罗来纳州，近 100 万人提前投票，这也是中期选举人数的创纪录数字。
据《亚特兰大宪法报》报道，佐治亚州也是如此，该州有超过 280 万人提前投票，比 2022 年中期选举增加了 13%，而 2022 年中期选举的提前投票人数创历史新高。
据美联社报道，缅因州、堪萨斯州、密歇根州的提前投票率也比 2022 年中期选举增加了 30% 以上。
2. 民主党展现提前投票实力
在美国各地，提前投票的民主党人远远多于共和党人。根据佛罗里达大学选举实验室的数据，民主党人投了 43% 的早期选票，而共和党人只投了 31%，无党派公民占选民投票率的 25%。
佛罗里达大学政治学家迈克尔·麦克唐纳 (Michael McDonald) 告诉 Axios，民主党人的参与程度高于共和党人，这可能反映出“对特朗普的公投”。
3.民主党比共和党获得更多支持
根据 PBS News/NPR/Marist 的一项民意调查，52% 的选民表示他们会支持所在选区的民主党国会候选人，而只有 44% 的人表示他们会支持共和党。
埃默里大学政治学教授伯纳德·弗拉加 (Bernard Fraga) 告诉《时代》杂志：“即使是坚定的共和党选民，他们也会关注经济状况，并表示自己对投票不太热衷。” “从趋势来看，很明显民主党人的热情和动员程度甚至比共和党选民还要高得多。”

Federal judge bars DoJ from threatening election workers to stop processing ballots
Order says local officials can’t be forced to separate or stop counting ballots that the government deems to be disputed
A federal judge has barred the justice department from threatening or coercing election workers to stop processing ballots.

The temporary restraining order issued by the US district judge Trina Thompson in the northern district of California late Friday also bars the justice department from demanding local election officials segregate or not count ballots that the federal government deems may have been illegally cast by immigrants, something that is exceedingly rare.
The order came the day after the justice department sent letters to election officials in all 50 states threatening to prosecute and jail any who failed to preserve ballot records.

The justice department’s “intimidation, threats, and attempts at coercion force election workers daily to choose between acceding to defendants’ unlawful demands or adhering to their duties and thereby subjecting themselves to a serious risk of criminal investigation and prosecution”. Thompson wrote.
The order in the lawsuit filed by labor unions and civil rights groups marks another blow to the Trump administration’s efforts to assert control over local elections.

It comes after a federal appeals court on Friday rejected the justice department’s request for California to set aside disputed ballots received in the midterm election, the latest setback for the Trump administration’s efforts to assert control over state-run elections.

The administration has alleged California sent ballots to about 20,000 people who may not be US citizens. It wants the state to set those ballots aside and not count them until citizenship can be verified. California officials say the list is highly unreliable and most likely includes many people who are US citizens.
A separate ruling from a three-judge panel on Wednesday forcefully denied that request, warning that the justice department’s demands could disenfranchise citizens.
Trump administration opens criminal investigation over alleged noncitizen voting in California

“As the district court found – and we discern no clear error – there is no feasible way to identify and segregate the ballots of specific individuals without potentially catastrophic effects on the entire system,” the ninth circuit court of appeals panel wrote in its 2-1 ruling.
The majority opinion was authored by Judge Mark J. Bennett, who was appointed by President Donald Trump, and Judge Gabriel P. Sanchez, who was appointed by former Ppresident Joe Biden.

A justice department spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the ruling. But in a statement about the sweeping efforts to root out noncitizen voting, it said: “Federal law prohibits noncitizens from voting. Enforcing that law is not an agenda item. It is the Department’s job.”

Two data scientists from the University of California, Los Angeles recently found that more than 40% of the ballots flagged by the Trump administration bear names that are not even found on the state’s voter rolls, according to the Associated Press. The researchers found that the Trump administration flagged thousands of voters as ineligible, despite the fact that their names corresponded with those of US citizens.

Millions of people have already voted in California in the midterm election that concludes on Tuesday. Hundreds of thousands of ballots have already been processed. Elections officials have said that processed votes can’t be matched back to the voters who submitted them.
The top federal prosecutor in Los Angeles, Bill Essayli, has said: “Any election official who knowingly processes the ballot of a noncitizen is opening themselves to legal jeopardy.”
body_zh: 联邦法官禁止司法部威胁选举工作人员停止处理选票美国新闻
联邦法官禁止司法部威胁选举工作人员停止处理选票
命令称，不得强迫地方官员分开或停止计票政府认为有争议的选票
一名联邦法官禁止司法部门威胁或强迫选举工作人员停止处理选票。
美国加州北区地区法官特里娜·汤普森周五晚间发布的临时限制令还禁止司法部要求地方选举官员隔离或不计票联邦政府认为可能由移民非法投票的选票，这种情况极其罕见。
就在该命令发布的第二天，司法部向所有 50 个州的选举官员发出了信函，威胁要起诉和监禁任何未能保存选票记录的人。
司法部门的“恐吓、威胁和胁迫企图迫使选举工作人员每天在接受被告的非法要求或坚守职责之间做出选择，从而使自己面临刑事调查和起诉的严重风险”。汤普森写道。
工会和民权组织提起的诉讼中的命令标志着对特朗普政府控制地方选举的努力的又一次打击。
此前，联邦上诉法院周五驳回了司法部要求加州搁置中期选举中收到的有争议选票的请求，这是特朗普政府试图控制州选举的最新挫折。
政府声称加州向大约 20,000 名可能不是美国公民的人发送了选票。它希望该州将这些选票放在一边，在公民身份得到验证之前不进行统计。加州官员表示，这份名单非常不可靠，而且很可能包括许多美国公民。
周三，由三名法官组成的小组做出的另一项裁决有力地驳回了这一请求，并警告司法部的要求可能会剥夺公民的公民权利。
特朗普政府对加州涉嫌非公民投票展开刑事调查
第九巡回上诉法院小组在其 2-1 裁决中写道：“正如地方法院所发现的那样，我们没有发现明显的错误，没有可行的方法来识别和隔离特定个人的选票，而不会对整个系统造成潜在的灾难性影响。”
多数意见由唐纳德·特朗普总统任命的马克·J·贝内特法官和前总统乔·拜登任命的加布里埃尔·P·桑切斯法官撰写。
司法部发言人没有立即回应对裁决发表评论的请求。但在一份关于根除非公民投票的全面努力的声明中，它表示：“联邦法律禁止非公民投票。执行该法律不是议程项目。这是该部门的工作。”
据美联社报道，加州大学洛杉矶分校的两名数据科学家最近发现，超过 40% 的特朗普政府标记的选票上的名字甚至没有出现在该州选民名册上。研究人员发现，特朗普政府将数千名选民标记为不符合资格，尽管他们的名字与美国公民的名字一致。
数百万人已经在加州周二结束的中期选举中投票。数十万张选票已经处理完毕。选举官员表示，处理过的选票无法与提交选票的选民进行匹配。
洛杉矶最高联邦检察官比尔·埃萨利 (Bill Essayli) 表示：“任何选举官员在知情的情况下处理非公民的选票，都会让自己面临法律风险。”

title_en: Politics chat: Data centers are on everyone's minds going into Election Day
title_zh: 政治聊天：进入选举日每个人都在关注数据中心
summary: With days until Election Day, polls show momentum for Democratic candidates and bipartisan distaste for data centers.
summary_zh: 距离选举日还有几天，民意调查显示了民主党候选人的势头以及两党对数据中心的厌恶。
body_en: Politics chat: Data centers are on everyone's minds going into Election Day : NPR
Politics chat: Data centers are on everyone's minds going into Election Day With days until Election Day, polls show momentum for Democratic candidates and bipartisan distaste for data centers.
Politics chat: Data centers are on everyone's minds going into Election Day
With days until Election Day, polls show momentum for Democratic candidates and bipartisan distaste for data centers.

Heading into this last weekend before Election Day, nearly 50 million people have already voted, either in person or by mail. The total vote in 2022's midterms was 112 million. This year's on pace to beat that number. NPR senior national political correspondent Mara Liasson joins us now. Good morning, Mara.
RASCOE: So where do things stand this morning from your point of view?

LIASSON: Well, Republicans and Democrats agree privately that the House will most likely go to the Democrats. It's unclear about the margin, probably a bigger one than the tiny majority that Republicans have now. Both sides say they are optimistic about the Senate. Of course, someone has to be wrong. Either Democrats will win the Senate majority, or Republicans will hold onto it.

The handful of races that are going to determine the majority in the Senate are all still polling within the margin of error. That means that they're too close to call. Democrats will probably pick up seats in the Senate, but it's not clear if they will get the net four pickups they need to take control. And the states that are going to determine that are Texas, Maine, Alaska, Ohio, Iowa and Kansas, a lot of red states.

RASCOE: Campaigns are making their final arguments, and, you know, those are going to vary race to race. In general, though, are there any issues that have risen to the top of voters' minds that stands out to you?

LIASSON: Yes, data centers. That was surprising. In the beginning of the cycle, it wasn't clear they would be such a big issue. States had been competing to get data centers to come to their states, but it turns out they are very unpopular. That sentiment is bipartisan. It's an example of the kind of economic populism that we see converging from the left and right. It's why you saw Bernie Sanders and Steve Bannon appear at the same anti-AI conference.

And data centers is the way that AI is most present to voters in their own communities. Majorities don't want them there. And it's caused some pretty dramatic flip-flops. Incumbent Texas Governor Greg Abbott courted data centers for years. All of a sudden, now he's for a moratorium.

And I think they've become a proxy for the backlash against billionaires. You know, the rich get richer while you can't afford gas. And the debate over the data centers also illustrates another big theme of the campaign, which is that Donald Trump is on the opposite side of majority popular opinion. On issue after issue, this is true - on Iran, on tariffs. On data centers, he says he's for them. He's called them a golden goose for the economy. He was in Ohio in October at a rally with Republican incumbent Senator Jon Husted. He said, we want data centers. He says, you can't turn them off. They'll go to China.
RASCOE: October has come and gone. Were there any so-called October surprises?

LIASSON: Well, I would say the closest thing to an October surprise is the double Dan Sullivan situation in Alaska. The Republican governor there says he's starting an investigation. President Trump has asked his Department of Justice to investigate how Daniel J. Sullivan got on the ballot. The incumbent senator is Dan S. Sullivan. There was some reporting in The New York Times that the Mary Peltola campaign - she's the Democratic candidate - was deeply involved in recruiting Dan J. Sullivan. Peltola denies that. The big question is, is any of this illegal?

RASCOE: I mean, that is a big question. Alaska's Supreme Court ruled in June that both Sullivans could appear on the ballot. And this is far from the first example of political parties, for lack of a better term, gaming the vote.

LIASSON: That's right. It happens a lot. Both parties do it. There are some examples this cycle. And one of them in Ohio, a Republican group, spent more than $2 million to promote a socialist candidate in the Senate race named Greg Levy. They're hoping to pull away votes from the Democratic candidate, former Senator Sherrod Brown.

So sometimes it's a person with a similar name, like in Alaska. Sometimes it's a person who's on the extreme of the opposite party, and the other party backs them in an effort to try to split the vote. Remember when Trump's allies tried to get Kanye West to run for president in hopes that he could split the Black vote? It's just unclear what, if any, laws these kinds of political shenanigans would break.
RASCOE: And yet the Justice Department is moving forward with its lawsuit about this, right?

LIASSON: That's right. They're asking a judge to separate all ballots in Alaska showing votes for the second Dan Sullivan, Dan J. Sullivan, until it can be determined if voters really meant to vote for him. Alaska officials say that would be impossible.

政治聊天：进入选举日，数据中心成为每个人关注的焦点 距离选举日还有几天，民意调查显示民主党候选人的势头强劲，而两党都对数据中心感到厌恶。
政治聊天：进入选举日每个人都在关注数据中心
距离选举日还有几天，民意调查显示了民主党候选人的势头以及两党对数据中心的厌恶。
截至选举日之前的最后一个周末，已有近 5000 万人亲自或通过邮寄投票。 2022年中期选举的总票数为1.12亿。今年有望打破这一数字。 NPR 高级国家政治记者 Mara Liasson 现在加入我们。早上好，玛拉。
拉斯科：那么从你的角度来看，今天早上的情况如何呢？
利亚森：嗯，共和党人和民主党人私下一致认为众议院很可能会落入民主党手中。目前还不清楚这一差距，可能比共和党现在拥有的微弱多数还要大。双方均表示对参议院持乐观态度。当然，一定有人是错的。要么民主党赢得参议院多数席位，要么共和党保住参议院多数席位。
少数几场将决定参议院多数席位的选举仍在误差范围内进行。这意味着他们的关系太接近了。民主党可能会在参议院获得席位，但尚不清楚他们是否能获得控制权所需的净四个席位。即将确定的州是德克萨斯州、缅因州、阿拉斯加、俄亥俄州、爱荷华州和堪萨斯州，这些都是红色州。
拉斯科：竞选活动正在做出最后的论点，而且，你知道，这些论点会因种族而异。不过，总的来说，有没有哪些问题是选民最关心的问题？
利亚森：是的，数据中心。这太令人惊讶了。在周期开始时，并不清楚它们会成为一个大问题。各州一直在竞相让数据中心落户本州，但事实证明它们非常不受欢迎。这种情绪是两党共同的。这是我们看到的左翼和右翼融合的经济民粹主义的一个例子。这就是为什么你会看到伯尼·桑德斯和史蒂夫·班农出现在同一个反人工智能会议上。
数据中心是人工智能在自己社区中向选民展示最多的方式。大多数人不希望他们在那里。这导致了一些非常戏剧性的转变。现任得克萨斯州州长格雷格·阿博特多年来一直在追求数据中心。突然之间，他要求暂停。

我认为他们已经成为针对亿万富翁的强烈抵制的代表。你知道，富人越来越富，而你却买不起汽油。关于数据中心的争论也说明了竞选活动的另一个大主题，那就是唐纳德·特朗普站在大多数民众观点的对立面。在一个又一个的问题上，这都是事实——在伊朗问题上，在关税问题上。在数据中心方面，他说他支持他们。他称它们为经济的金鹅。 10 月份，他在俄亥俄州与共和党现任参议员乔恩·赫斯特德 (Jon Husted) 一起参加集会。他说，我们想要数据中心。他说，你不能把它们关掉。他们会去中国。
拉斯科：十月已经过去了。有所谓的十月惊喜吗？

利亚森：嗯，我想说，最接近十月惊喜的是阿拉斯加的双重丹·沙利文事件。那里的共和党州长表示他正在开始调查。特朗普总统已要求司法部调查丹尼尔·J·沙利文 (Daniel J. Sullivan) 是如何参与投票的。现任参议员是丹·S·沙利文。 《纽约时报》有报道称，民主党候选人玛丽·佩尔托拉（Mary Peltola）竞选团队深入参与了丹·J·沙利文（Dan J. Sullivan）的招募。佩尔托拉否认了这一点。最大的问题是，这是否违法？
拉斯科：我的意思是，这是一个大问题。阿拉斯加最高法院六月裁定，苏利文夫妇都可以参加投票。由于缺乏更好的术语，这远不是政党操纵选票的第一个例子。
利亚森：没错。这种事经常发生。双方都这样做。这个周期有一些例子。其中俄亥俄州的一个共和党团体花费超过 200 万美元在参议院竞选中宣传一位名叫格雷格·利维 (Greg Levy) 的社会主义候选人。他们希望夺走民主党候选人、前参议员谢罗德·布朗的选票。
所以有时是一个名字相似的人，比如在阿拉斯加。有时是一个人站在对方的极端，对方支持他，试图分裂选票。还记得特朗普的盟友试图让坎耶·韦斯特竞选总统，希望他能平分黑人选票吗？目前还不清楚这些政治恶作剧会违反哪些法律（如果有的话）。
拉斯科：然而司法部正在就此提起诉讼，对吗？
利亚森：没错。他们要求法官将阿拉斯加所有投票给第二任丹·沙利文（Dan J. Sullivan）的选票分开，直到确定选民是否真的打算投票给他。阿拉斯加官员表示这是不可能的。

title_en: What NPR's senior political correspondent is watching for on Election Night
title_zh: NPR 的高级政治记者在选举之夜关注什么
summary: An NPR senior political editor/correspondent tells us what he will be looking out for as results roll in on Election Day.
summary_zh: NPR 的一位高级政治编辑/记者告诉我们，随着选举日结果的公布，他将关注什么。
body_en: What NPR's senior political correspondent is watching for on Election Night : NPR
What NPR's senior political correspondent is watching for on Election Night An NPR senior political editor/correspondent tells us what he will be looking out for as results roll in on Election Day.
What NPR's senior political correspondent is watching for on Election Night
An NPR senior political editor/correspondent tells us what he will be looking out for as results roll in on Election Day.

As the old cliche goes, the only poll that matters is the one on Election Day. Domenico Montanaro is NPR's senior political editor and correspondent, and he joins us now to talk about what he'll be watching for as the results roll in on Tuesday. Hi there, Domenico.
DOMENICO MONTANARO, BYLINE: Great to be with you. Let's go.
RASCOE: As polls start to close on Tuesday, what will you be looking for in the early results?

MONTANARO: Yeah. I mean, one of the big things I'm watching on election night is Republican turnout. If Republicans have a high level of turnout on election night, that could really mitigate some of these Democratic gains that are expected. If they have a low turnout, then we could see a real washout across the country.

So early on, we're going to start to see results come in in the 6 p.m. Eastern time hour. And two races I'm particularly watching are the 5th Congressional District in Indiana and the 6th Congressional District in Kentucky because Kentucky is a close race. And we're not sure which way it's going to be going, and we're going to see what those margins are. In Indiana 5 - that's incumbent Victoria Spartz's district - she's expected to win. But if she's in a tighter race than expected, look out for the rest of the night and for what that could mean for the House.

Also, in Florida - Florida, also, we're going to see a lot of results start to come in fairly early on. And, you know, look at a place like Florida 22. That is a huge Latino population. If you're seeing Democrats do well in a place like that, that could mean a big sweep across South Florida and South Texas for what we see later on.
RASCOE: We'll have a lot of races closing at 9 p.m. Eastern time. How will your focus have shifted by that time?

MONTANARO: From a trickle to a fire hose. I mean, at 9 p.m., we're looking at Arizona, Colorado, Iowa, Louisiana, Minnesota, Nebraska, New Mexico, New York, Wisconsin and Wyoming. All will have results coming in. And we're going to really have a good sense, especially in the House, 'cause it's only a three-seat majority for Republicans. We're going to start to get a real sense of whether or not Democrats take over the House in the 9 p.m. hour.

RASCOE: Talk to me about the Senate. There's lots of news about lots of races. The president is in Iowa and Kansas today. Alaska is competitive. Will we have to wait until the last polls close there, well past midnight Eastern time, to know which party controls the Senate?
MONTANARO: God, you are giving me my worst-nightmare scenario...

MONTANARO: ...Which is quite possible because Alaska is one of those places that is looking really close right now - a toss-up state, a red state that Trump won but looks very, very close, and it counts votes very, very slowly. It has rank-choice voting. They didn't decide their races sometimes till three weeks later. If we're stuck in a mess of three weeks waiting to know control of the Senate, there's going to be a whole heck of a lot of misinformation going on. We know that President Trump's already laying the groundwork to say that the election was rigged. You know, it's better to have decisive victories one way or the other in this country because close elections tend to now be contested.

But look. You've got five toss-up seats that are in red states, all places Trump won by double digits in the 2024 presidential election. And again, here's where Republican turnout is really going to matter. If Trump can get that base out, you know, you could be looking at a one- or two-seat Democratic net pickup in the Senate. And remember, they need four seats to take control of the Senate. If Republican turnout's not great, you know, you could be looking at six or seven seats that go toward Democrats.
RASCOE: When you watch the exit polls come in, what will you be looking for in what people are saying they care about?

MONTANARO: Yeah. There's a couple of numbers that I'm looking for. No. 1, when it comes to 18- to 29-year-olds, you know, they turn out at a very low percentage in midterm elections. They have - they see the steepest drop-off from presidential elections of any subgroup. And I'm looking to see if Democrats can win young voters by more than 20 points. I think that margin is going to be really key.

I'm also looking for how Latinos wind up voting in, again, South Florida and South Texas. Remember, Trump won 46% of them in the 2024 presidential election, the highest ever for a Republican presidential candidate. They have been really soured on Trump, according to polls - 27% approval rating, for example, in the latest NBC Telemundo poll. And finally, the third thing I would look for is the number 46% when it comes to how Republicans do with independents. In the Trump era, when Republicans have gotten 46% or more with independents, they've seen success. When they've been below that, in two elections, they have not - 2018 and 2020.
body_zh: NPR 的高级政治记者在选举之夜关注什么 : NPR
NPR 的高级政治记者在选举之夜关注什么 NPR 的高级政治编辑/通讯员告诉我们，随着选举日结果的公布，他将关注什么。
NPR 的高级政治记者在选举之夜关注什么
NPR 的一位高级政治编辑/记者告诉我们，随着选举日结果的公布，他将关注什么。
正如一句老话所说，唯一重要的民意调查是选举日的民意调查。多梅尼科·蒙塔纳罗 (Domenico Montanaro) 是 NPR 的高级政治编辑和记者，他现在加入我们，谈论周二结果公布时他将关注的内容。你好，多梅尼科。
多梅尼科·蒙塔纳罗连线：很高兴和你在一起。我们走吧。
拉斯科：随着周二投票开始结束，您会在早期结果中寻找什么？
蒙塔纳罗：是的。我的意思是，我在选举之夜关注的最重要的事情之一就是共和党的投票率。如果共和党在选举之夜的投票率很高，那确实可能会削弱民主党的一些预期收益。如果他们的投票率低，那么我们可能会在全国范围内看到真正的淘汰。
所以一早就开始，我们将在下午 6 点开始看到结果。东部时间。我特别关注的两场比赛是印第安纳州第五国会选区和肯塔基州第六国会选区，因为肯塔基州是一场势均力敌的比赛。我们不确定它会朝哪个方向发展，我们将看看这些利润是多少。在印第安纳州第五区——现任维多利亚·斯巴茨的选区——她有望获胜。但如果她的竞选比预期更激烈，请留意今晚剩下的时间以及这对众议院意味着什么。
此外，在佛罗里达州，我们也将看到很多结果很早就开始出现。而且，你知道，看看像佛罗里达 22 这样的地方。那里有大量拉丁裔人口。如果你看到民主党在这样的地方表现出色，这可能意味着我们稍后会看到南佛罗里达州和南德克萨斯州的大胜。
拉斯科：我们将有很多比赛在晚上 9 点结束。东部时间。到那时你的注意力将如何转移？
蒙塔纳罗：从细流到消防水带。我的意思是，晚上 9 点，我们将关注亚利桑那州、科罗拉多州、爱荷华州、路易斯安那州、明尼苏达州、内布拉斯加州、新墨西哥州、纽约州、威斯康星州和怀俄明州。一切都会有结果。我们将会有很好的判断力，尤其是在众议院，因为共和党只获得三个席位。我们将开始真正了解民主党是否会在晚上 9 点接管众议院。小时。
拉斯科：跟我谈谈参议院。有很多关于很多比赛的新闻。总统今天在爱荷华州和堪萨斯州。阿拉斯加很有竞争力。我们是否必须等到最后一次民意调查结束，即东部时间午夜过后，才能知道哪个政党控制着参议院？
蒙塔纳罗：上帝，你正在给我带来最可怕的噩梦场景......

蒙塔纳罗：……这很有可能，因为阿拉斯加是目前看起来非常接近的地方之一——一个摇摆不定的州，一个特朗普获胜但看起来非常非常接近的红色州，而且计票速度非常非常慢。它有排名选择投票。有时他们直到三周后才决定参加比赛。如果我们陷入混乱的三周等待知道参议院的控制权，就会出现大量错误信息。我们知道特朗普总统已经为说选举被操纵奠定了基础。你知道，在这个国家，最好以某种方式取得决定性的胜利，因为现在的选举往往是势均力敌的。
但你看。红色州有 5 个席位悬而未决，特朗普在 2024 年总统选举中以两位数的优势赢得了这些席位。再说一次，这就是共和党的投票率真正重要的地方。如果特朗普能够赢得这个基础，你知道，你可能会看到民主党在参议院净增加一个或两个席位。请记住，他们需要四个席位才能控制参议院。如果共和党的投票率不是很高，你知道，你可能会看到六七个席位被民主党占据。
拉斯科：当你看到出口民调结果时，你会从人们所说的他们关心的事情中寻找什么？
蒙塔纳罗：是的。我正在寻找几个数字。第一，对于 18 至 29 岁的人来说，你知道，他们在中期选举中的投票率非常低。他们看到了所有分组中总统选举中跌幅最大的。我想看看民主党能否以超过 20 个百分点的优势赢得年轻选民的支持。我认为利润率将是非常关键的。

我还在寻找拉丁美洲人如何最终在南佛罗里达州和南德克萨斯州投票。请记住，特朗普在 2024 年总统选举中赢得了 46% 的支持率，这是共和党总统候选人有史以来最高的支持率。民意调查显示，他们对特朗普真的很不满——例如，在最新的 NBC Telemundo 民意调查中，他们的支持率为 27%。最后，我要寻找的第三件事是，当谈到共和党人如何对待独立人士时，46% 的数字。在特朗普时代，当共和党获得无党派支持率 46% 或更多时，他们就看到了成功。当他们在 2018 年和 2020 年的两次选举中都没有低于这一水平时。

title_en: Living with high prices in Virginia's 1st Congressional District
title_zh: 弗吉尼亚州第一国会选区的高物价生活
summary: High prices are straining budgets for both a small business owner and a single mom in a rural part of Va.'s 1st Congressional district. They explain how they're handling the economic stress of these times.
summary_zh: 高物价使弗吉尼亚州第一国会选区农村地区的小企业主和单亲妈妈的预算紧张。他们解释了
body_en: Living with high prices in Virginia's 1st Congressional District : NPR

Living with high prices in Virginia's 1st Congressional District High prices are straining budgets for both a small business owner and a single mom in a rural part of Va.'s 1st Congressional district. They explain how they're handling the economic stress of these times.
Living with high prices in Virginia's 1st Congressional District
Residents of Virginia's 1st Congressional District on living with high prices
A mural off Tappahannock's main road, in the courtyard next to the Java Jacks Cafe Melissa Gray/NPR hide caption
A display of t-shirts at Java Jacks Cafe in Tappahannock, Virginia Melissa Gray/NPR hide caption

At Java Jacks in the riverside town of Tappahannock, Va., the sausage is savory, the beignet-like jacks are sugar-dusted and you have your choice of t-shirts. You can get a brightly-colored one with an image of the cafe and its slogan, "Come in, We're Awesome," or you can go for something darkly funny that says "Coffee Makes Me Feel Less Murdery."

"We started by selling just the t-shirts of the building. And then we'd gotten a couple of the sarcastic shirts for the staff and the customers were trying to buy them off of our backs," owner Jeans Owens laughs from behind the coffee bar. Java Jacks started in 2006, in what was once someone's little one-story home on the main road through town. The atmosphere is cozy and friendly, with pictures of smiling customers and staff taped to door frames and to the wall.
Snapshots of happy staff and customers decorate the walls and doors of Java Jacks Melissa Gray/NPR hide caption

Owens and her husband took over the business about eight years ago. "What we were interested in was being our own bosses," she says, "and something that could set us up a little better for retirement."
But their first years running the cafe have included the pandemic and inflation: lots of expensive bumps for small business owners.

"Our coffee prices went sky high," she says. They're up over 30% since 2022. The cost of beef is up, so is the cost of sausage and paper products for takeout orders: "To-go boxes. You know there was a time we were paying 12 cents for those," Owens says. Now, it's nearly 30 cents. And to-go cups? "The cup, the lid, the straw used to cost us all together maybe 3 cents." She says it's now more than 20 cents.
The cafe's electricity bill has also recently jumped. "Normally, I'm paying $450, $500 a month," she says. "I'm paying over $1000 now."

Owens says Java Jacks has a loyal customer base and she's been committed to doing whatever she can to keep menu prices affordable, including keeping some meals at $10. She says she now goes to Walmart early in the morning to get milk and juice rather than purchase them from a supplier. She goes to a local grocery store for fresh fruit. She also regularly checks prices between three suppliers and switches between them, depending on which one has the lowest costs.

It's not just Owens' habits that have changed, it's her customers': she's noticed more senior citizens sharing orders. "We had like maybe one or two when we bought [Java Jacks], but now we'll have multiple tickets a day that are split." Some customers are adjusting how they tip her staff, too. "They tend to be tipped very well just because we're a small atmosphere," Owens says. But when the price of gas shot up, the tips got smaller. "When [gas] came back down, we started seeing that trend change," she says.
From behind the coffee bar, cafe owner Jeans Owens shows NPR's Ayesha Rascoe the Java Jacks menu Melissa Gray/NPR hide caption

Owens feels she's handling the increase in costs as best she can, though she is having to increase menu prices. But the biggest stressor for her right now is finding and keeping staff, a situation that's also rooted in affordability. Owens has another coffee spot across the river in Warsaw. She's been short-staffed between both locations for months at a time. Rents have increased in this rural area, where the median income is around $50,000 a year. She says she's had to help employees find places to live and she's even put them up temporarily in a motel. Transportation is another problem: some workers don't have cars or are squeezed too much by current gas prices. "We have about five employees right now that we carpool to work," she says.

All of this means Owens has had to take shifts in the kitchen, putting off her front-of-house duties and paperwork to her evenings and days off. She says it's the same with other local restaurant owners: they're working themselves to the bone.

Owens won't discuss midterm politics, even though what she's learned about the lack of housing and transportation in the area has prompted her to run for the non-partisan town council. Tappahannock is in the eastern part of Virginia's 1st Congressional District, where the race between long-time Republican incumbent Rob Wittman and Democrat Shannon Taylor, the commonwealth's attorney for Henrico County, has been tight. Owens says whoever wins, she wants them to understand what small businesses like hers are dealing with these days. "We're struggling," she says, bluntly.
Jameka Campbell, who works across the river in Richmond County, thinks politicians are out of touch with the today's economic reality.
body_zh: 弗吉尼亚州第一国会选区的高物价生活：NPR
弗吉尼亚州第一国会选区的高物价生活 对于弗吉尼亚州第一国会选区农村地区的小企业主和单亲妈妈来说，高物价使预算紧张。他们解释了他们如何应对当前的经济压力。
弗吉尼亚州第一国会选区的高物价生活
弗吉尼亚第一国会选区居民面临高物价生活
塔帕汉诺克主干道旁 Java Jacks 咖啡馆旁边的庭院中的一幅壁画 Melissa Gray/NPR 隐藏标题栏
弗吉尼亚州塔帕汉诺克的 Java Jacks 咖啡馆展示的 T 恤 Melissa Gray/NPR 隐藏标题栏
在弗吉尼亚州塔帕汉诺克河畔小镇的 Java Jacks，香肠味道鲜美，贝奈特状的 Jacks 撒满了糖，您还可以选择自己喜欢的 T 恤。你可以买一张颜色鲜艳的咖啡，上面有咖啡馆的图片和它的口号“进来，我们很棒”，或者你也可以选择一些黑色有趣的咖啡，上面写着“咖啡让我感觉不那么谋杀”。
“一开始我们只卖大楼里的 T 恤。然后我们给员工买了几件带有讽刺意味的 T 恤，顾客们试图从我们这里买下来，”店主 Jeans Owens 在咖啡吧后面笑着说。 Java Jacks 成立于 2006 年，地点曾经是一个位于穿过城镇的主干道上的单层小房子。气氛舒适而友好，门框和墙上贴着微笑的顾客和员工的照片。
Java Jacks 的墙壁和门上装饰着快乐的员工和顾客的快照 Melissa Gray/NPR 隐藏标题栏
大约八年前，欧文斯和她的丈夫接管了这家公司。 “我们感兴趣的是成为自己的老板，”她说，“以及能让我们更好地退休的事情。”
但他们经营这家咖啡馆的第一年经历了流行病和通货膨胀：小企业主面临许多昂贵​​的障碍。
“我们的咖啡价格飞得很高，”她说。自 2022 年以来，价格上涨了 30% 以上。牛肉的成本上涨了，外卖订单中的香肠和纸制品的成本也上涨了：“外卖盒。你知道，曾经我们为这些东西支付 12 美分，”欧文斯说。现在，已经接近30美分了。还有外带杯子？ “杯子、盖子和吸管总共花了我们 3 美分。”她说现在已经超过20美分了。
咖啡馆的电费最近也大幅上涨。 “通常情况下，我每月支付 450 至 500 美元，”她说。 “我现在要付1000多美元。”
欧文斯说，Java Jacks 拥有忠实的客户群，她一直致力于尽一切努力保持菜单价格实惠，包括将一些餐点保持在 10 美元。她说她现在一大早就去沃尔玛买牛奶和果汁，而不是从供应商那里购买。她去当地的一家杂货店买新鲜水果。她还定期检查三个供应商之间的价格，并根据哪一个供应商的成本最低进行切换。
改变的不仅仅是欧文斯的习惯，还有她的顾客：她注意到更多的老年人分享订单。 “当我们购买 [Java Jacks] 时，我们可能只有一两张，但现在我们每天会有多张分开的门票。”一些顾客也在调整给员工小费的方式。欧文斯说：“因为我们的氛围很小，他们往往会得到很好的小费。”但当汽油价格飙升时，小费就变小了。 “当[天然气]回落时，我们开始看到趋势发生变化，”她说。
在咖啡吧后面，咖啡馆老板 Jeans Owens 向 NPR 的 Ayesha Rascoe 展示 Java Jacks 菜单 Melissa Gray/NPR 隐藏标题栏

欧文斯认为，尽管她不得不提高菜单价格，但她正在尽力应对成本的增加。但她目前面临的最大压力是寻找和留住员工，这种情况也源于负担能力。欧文斯在华沙河对岸还有另一家咖啡馆。几个月来，她在这两个地点之间一直人手短缺。这个农村地区的租金上涨了，那里的年收入中位数约为 50,000 美元。她说她必须帮助员工找到住处，甚至把他们暂时安置在汽车旅馆里。交通是另一个问题：一些工人没有汽车，或者受到当前汽油价格的挤压。 “我们现在大约有五名员工，我们拼车上班，”她说。
所有这一切意味着欧文斯不得不在厨房轮班，将前台职责和文书工作推迟到晚上和休息日。她说，这与当地其他餐馆老板一样：他们正在拼命工作。
欧文斯不会讨论中期政治，尽管她了解到该地区缺乏住房和交通，促使她竞选无党派镇议会议员。塔帕汉诺克位于弗吉尼亚州第一国会选区的东部，长期任职的共和党议员罗布·威特曼 (Rob Wittman) 和民主党人、亨利科县联邦检察官香农·泰勒 (Shannon Taylor) 之间的竞争一直很激烈。欧文斯说，无论谁获胜，她都希望他们了解像她这样的小企业如今正在应对什么。 “我们正在挣扎，”她直言不讳地说。
在河对岸的里士满县工作的贾梅卡·坎贝尔 (Jameka Campbell) 认为政客们与当今的经济现实脱节。

body_en: Democrat Haley Stevens endorses Abdul El-Sayed’s Republican rival Mike Rogers
Endorsement was met with backlash from the party, condemning Stevens for her ‘betrayal’

Congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost the Michigan Democratic Senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed, endorsed his Republican rival, Mike Rogers, in an extraordinary rebuke of her party’s nominee on the eve of the midterm elections.

Her endorsement came in a video posted to X after she attended an event with Rogers at the predominantly Black Perfecting church in Detroit on Sunday. Stevens’s endorsement was the culmination of an escalating feud between the former primary rivals – primarily over support for Israel – that has roiled one of the most fiercely contested Senate contests of the cycle.
The endorsement was met with immediate pushback from Democrats , who condemned Stevens for her “betrayal”.

Michigan’s Democratic party chair Curtis Hertel said: “Haley Stevens’ decision to campaign with Rogers – a man who has repeatedly sold out Michigan’s working class, wants to pass a national abortion ban, and has pledged to be a loyal vote for Trump’s agenda – shows that she has abandoned everything she claims to care about. We reject the attempts by Stevens and bad-faith actors to divide our party and undermine our momentum, and will not allow these eleventh-hour distractions deter us.”

Some of the people who worked for Stevens’s campaign also reportedly quit following her Rogers endorsement. Her long-time chief of staff, Justin German, and her communications director, Logan Basch, were among those who left, according to CNN correspondent Manu Raju.

German later released a statement on behalf of Stevens’ campaign team endorsing El-Sayed: “As Haley Stevens’ Chief of staff for eight years, I speak on behalf of our team in wholeheartedly supporting Abdul El-Sayed for Senate. This election is too important to sow division or stand on the sidelines. We are shocked and heartbroken by Congresswoman Stevens’ decision to support Mike Rogers.”
Fallout over Stevens’ endorsement of Rogers continued Sunday, with figures from the progressive left stepping up to back El-Sayed.

Bernie Sanders joined the controversy, attacking Stevens for what Democrats view as an extraordinary betrayal after Stevens accepted El-Sayed’s narrow victory over her in Michigan’s Democrat senate primaries.

“Rep. Haley Stevens’ staff is right to resign in disgust,” Sanders posted on X. “They understand that the election in Michigan is far more important than Haley’s fragile ego and that all of us must stand together to elect Abdul, defeat Rogers and end the Republican rubber-stamp control of the Senate.”
Zohran Mamdani, the New York City mayor, said Stevens had “betrayed” working class people “by endorsing the very Republican she said she wanted to run against”.

In his first public comments since Stevens’s endorsement of Rogers, El-Sayed told reporters at a press conference outside of a rally he held on Sunday, the very same rally that Stevens had earlier been disinvited from attending, “At the end of the day, I actually don’t think about Haley Stevens.” He added, “I’m just less interested in the politics of it all than I am in the policy of it all.

“If you are somebody who believes that we should stand up to hate, and you have watched this last campaign, I think we probably would not want to support Mike Rogers and Donald Trump and JD Vance,” he said.
But Stevens’s political pivot earned her praise from Donald Trump, someone whose policies she has an entire page on her website dedicated to denouncing.

Trump, during his rally in Iowa, heaped praise on Stevens for turning against El-Sayed, urging her to join the GOP. “It was an incredible thing,” Trump said. “I’d love her to join the Republican party. I think that could happen.”

Stevens had lost by a close margin in this year’s primary, and for months had refused to openly campaign for El-Sayed, as had his other opponent Mallory McMorrow. But top Democrats had brokered the truce between El-Sayed and Stevens. After the two had sparred viciously in the primary campaign Stevens extended him a tepid endorsement, and this weekend was scheduled to join El-Sayed at a predominantly Black church in Detroit’s North End.
Haley Stevens advised to stay away from Abdul El-Sayed campaign events to limit ‘distractions’
Those plans have quickly unraveled over an issue that divided Stevens and El-Sayed perhaps more than any other: Israel.

Later last week, Stevens, a staunch supporter of Israel, made clear that her appearance alongside El-Sayed was preconditioned on his denouncing of an outside group’s campaign ad that had blamed US support of Israel for the rising cost of living. El-Sayed declined the request, accusing Stevens of needlessly reopening debates from a settled primary.
body_zh: 民主党人海莉·史蒂文斯支持阿卜杜勒·赛义德的共和党对手迈克·罗杰斯
支持遭到党内强烈反对，谴责史蒂文斯的“背叛”
在密歇根州民主党参议院初选中输给阿卜杜勒·赛义德的国会女议员海莉·史蒂文斯在中期选举前夕对共和党提名人进行了非同寻常的谴责，她支持了他的共和党竞争对手迈克·罗杰斯。
周日，她与罗杰斯一起参加了在底特律以黑人为主的完美教堂举行的活动后，她在 X 上发布了一段视频，对此表示支持。史蒂文斯的支持是前初选竞争对手之间不断升级的不和（主要是因为对以色列的支持）的顶峰，这场争斗已经搅乱了本周期竞争最激烈的参议院竞选之一。
这一支持立即遭到民主党人的反对，他们谴责史蒂文斯的“背叛”。
密歇根州民主党主席柯蒂斯·赫特尔表示：“海莉·史蒂文斯决定与罗杰斯一起竞选。罗杰斯曾多次出卖密歇根州的工人阶级，希望通过全国堕胎禁令，并承诺为特朗普的议程提供忠诚的一票。这表明她已经放弃了她声称关心的一切。我们拒绝史蒂文斯和不怀好意的演员分裂我们党、破坏我们势头的企图，也不会允许这些最后一刻的干扰阻止我们。”
据报道，一些为史蒂文斯竞选活动工作的人在她支持罗杰斯后也辞职了。据美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 记者马努·拉朱 (Manu Raju) 报道，长期担任她的幕僚长贾斯汀·日尔曼 (Justin German) 和通讯总监洛根·巴什 (Logan Basch) 都在离职之列。
杰曼后来代表史蒂文斯的竞选团队发表声明，支持艾尔赛义德：“作为海莉·史蒂文斯的八年幕僚长，我代表我们的团队全心全意支持阿卜杜勒·艾尔赛义德竞选参议员。这次选举太重要了，不能制造分裂或袖手旁观。我们对国会女议员史蒂文斯支持迈克·罗杰斯的决定感到震惊和心碎。”
周日，史蒂文斯支持罗杰斯的余波仍在继续，进步左派人士站出来支持埃尔-赛义德。
伯尼·桑德斯也加入了这场争议，在史蒂文斯接受了埃尔-赛义德在密歇根州民主党参议院初选中以微弱优势战胜她之后，民主党人认为史蒂文斯是一种非同寻常的背叛，并攻击史蒂文斯。
桑德斯在 X 上发帖称：“众议员海莉·史蒂文斯的工作人员厌恶地辞职是正确的。他们明白，密歇根州的选举比海莉脆弱的自我重要得多，我们所有人必须团结起来，选举阿卜杜勒，击败罗杰斯，结束共和党对参议院的橡皮图章控制。”
纽约市市长佐兰·马姆达尼 (Zohran Mamdani) 表示，史蒂文斯“支持她声称要竞选的共和党人”，从而“背叛”了工人阶级人民。
自从史蒂文斯支持罗杰斯以来，埃尔赛义德在他周日举行的一次集会外的新闻发布会上对记者表示，这是他自史蒂文斯支持罗杰斯以来的首次公开评论，史蒂文斯早些时候被取消参加同一集会，“归根结底，我实际上并没有想到海莉·史蒂文斯。”他补充道：“我对这一切的政治不太感兴趣，而对这一切的政策更感兴趣。
“如果你认为我们应该勇敢地面对仇恨，并且你观看了上一次竞选活动，我想我们可能不想支持迈克·罗杰斯、唐纳德·特朗普和 JD·万斯，”他说。
但史蒂文斯的政治立场为她赢得了唐纳德·特朗普的赞扬，她在自己的网站上用整个页面专门谴责特朗普的政策。
特朗普在爱荷华州的集会上盛赞史蒂文斯反对埃尔赛义德，敦促她加入共和党。 “这是一件令人难以置信的事情，”特朗普说。 “我希望她加入共和党。我认为这可能会发生。”
史蒂文斯在今年的初选中以微弱优势落败，几个月来一直拒绝公开为埃尔赛义德竞选，他的另一位对手马洛里·麦克莫罗也是如此。但民主党高层促成了埃尔赛义德和史蒂文斯之间的休战。两人在初选中发生了激烈的争吵后，史蒂文斯对他表示了不温不火的支持，并计划本周末与埃尔赛义德一起前往底特律北端的一座以黑人为主的教堂。
海莉·史蒂文斯建议远离阿卜杜勒·赛义德的竞选活动，以限制“分心”
这些计划很快就因一个问题而瓦解，这个问题可能是史蒂文斯和埃尔-赛义德之间最严重的分歧：以色列。
上周晚些时候，以色列的坚定支持者史蒂文斯明确表示，她与埃尔赛义德一起露面的前提是他谴责一个外部团体的竞选广告，该广告将生活成本上升归咎于美国对以色列的支持。埃尔-赛义德拒绝了这一请求，指责史蒂文斯不必要地在已经确定的初选后重新开启辩论。

title_en: Do you know signs of a stroke? BE FAST are the words to remember
title_zh: 你知道中风的征兆吗？要记住的话要快
summary: Sen. Chris Murphy is expected to fully recover from his stroke. The acronym BE FAST can help you remember the symptoms of stroke and what to do when it happens: Call 911 quickly.
summary_zh: 参议员克里斯·墨菲预计将从中风中完全康复。首字母缩略词“BE FAST”可以帮助您记住中风的症状以及当我发生中风时该怎么办
body_en: BE FAST to help someone survive a stroke : NPR

BE FAST to help someone survive a stroke Sen. Chris Murphy is expected to fully recover from his stroke. The acronym BE FAST can help you remember the symptoms of stroke and what to do when it happens: Call 911 quickly.
Do you know signs of a stroke? BE FAST are the words to remember
Sen. Chris Murphy, D-Conn., speaks to reporters in March 2026, in Washington. Murphy suffered a stroke on Saturday and is expected to recover. Allison Robbert/AP hide caption
Sen. Chris Murphy, D-Conn., suffered a stroke on Saturday. His prognosis is excellent, according to his office. His case illustrates the importance of knowing the warning signs of a stroke.
The American Stroke Association says following the six letters in the acronym BE FAST — can help save stroke victims and prevent permanent brain damage.
Connecticut Senator Chris Murphy is hospitalized with a stroke

Murphy, 53, had the "A" for "arm weakness" — he felt numbness in his arm while he was at his son's hockey game, according to a statement from his staff. And they said he acted quickly to get care — that's the "T" for "time."
Being seen by medical professionals as soon as possible — be fast! — gives people the best shot at survival and full recovery.
Here are all six of the stroke-spotting signs in the BE FAST acronym, according to the American Stroke Association
Dizzyness, trouble walking or a sudden loss of balance are all signs that a stroke may be occurring.
Is the person having trouble with their vision? Blurred vision, double vision or loss of sight in one eye are important symptoms.
Ask the person to smile. Is their smile uneven? Numbness or drooping on one side of the face is a symptom.
Numbness in one arm, as Murphy had, is a symptom. Weakness is too. Ask the person to raise both arms. Does one arm drift down?
Trouble talking is another common symptom. Can the person repeat a simple sentence? Is their speech slurred or hard to understand?
If you or someone you are with is experiencing these symptoms, call 911 as soon as you can. Getting care quickly is very important for survival and to minimize long-term effects.

A stroke happens when blood flow to or within the brain is interrupted. It can happen when an artery is blocked or when a blood vessel in the brain bursts. Brain tissue that is deprived of oxygen can be permanently damaged, resulting in long-term disability or death.
Heart disease deaths declined. And here's how to reduce your risk of the #1 killer
Other important symptoms of a stroke are a severe headache, confusion and numbness on one side of the body.
Stroke is the #4 leading cause of death in the U.S., killing more than 162,000 people in 2023, according to the American Heart Association.

康涅狄格州民主党参议员克里斯·墨菲周六中风。据他的办公室称，他的预后良好。他的案例说明了了解中风警告信号的重要性。
美国中风协会表示，遵循缩写词“BE FAST”中的六个字母可以帮助拯救中风患者并防止永久性脑损伤。
康涅狄格州参议员克里斯·墨菲因中风住院
墨菲，53 岁，“A”代表“手臂无力”——根据他的工作人员的一份声明，他在观看儿子的曲棍球比赛时感到手臂麻木。他们说他迅速采取行动以获得护理——这是“时间”的“T”。
尽快让医疗专业人员就诊——动作要快！ — 为人们提供生存和全面康复的最佳机会。
根据美国中风协会的说法，以下是 BE FAST 缩写中的所有六个中风发现标志
头晕、行走困难或突然失去平衡都是可能发生中风的迹象。
此人的视力有问题吗？视力模糊、复视或一只眼睛失明是重要的症状。
请对方微笑。他们的笑容是否参差不齐？面部一侧麻木或下垂是一种症状。
像墨菲那样，一只手臂麻木是一种症状。弱点也是。请对方举起双臂。一只手臂会向下垂吗？
说话困难是另一个常见症状。这个人可以重复一个简单的句子吗？他们的言语是否含糊不清或难以理解？
如果您或您身边的人出现这些症状，请尽快拨打 911。快速获得护理对于生存和最大限度地减少长期影响非常重要。
当流向大脑或大脑内部的血液中断时，就会发生中风。当动脉阻塞或脑部血管破裂时，就会发生这种情况。缺氧的脑组织可能会受到永久性损伤，导致长期残疾或死亡。

中风的其他重要症状包括严重头痛、意识模糊和身体一侧麻木。

title_zh: 佛罗里达州坠毁的公务机上九人全部遇难
summary: Aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom international airport and was headed to the Bahamas when it crashed All nine people have died who were aboard a business jet that crashed in a Florida neighborhood on Sunday, Sean Duffy, the US transportation secretary, s
summary_zh: 飞机从奥斯汀-博格斯多姆国际机场起飞，前往巴哈马时坠毁，机上九人全部遇难。
body_en: All nine people aboard business jet that crashed in Florida have died | Florida
All nine people aboard business jet that crashed in Florida have died
Aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom international airport and was headed to the Bahamas when it crashed

All nine people have died who were aboard a business jet that crashed in a Florida neighborhood on Sunday, Sean Duffy, the US transportation secretary, said. The aircraft erupted in a massive fireball that appeared to just miss homes before crashing near a busy roadway.

Duffy posted on X on Sunday that the Learjet 60 crashed in Palm Beach county at 12.50pm and called it a “horrific tragedy”. The Federal Aviation Administration is sending a team to support the National Transportation Safety Board’s investigation into the cause, he said.

The aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom international airport in Texas and was headed to the Bahamas, according to the Federal Aviation Administration. Authorities did not immediately say what caused the jet to go down or who was on it.
Jim Reynolds, a spokesperson for the airport, said it was a private aircraft. He could not immediately provide details about who was on the flight.
He said the tail number for the flight was N722BD.

Video shot from people inside their cars captured the terrifying moment the aircraft plunged from the sky, before striking near the roadway and exploding. Flames flickered around chunks of pavement lining the crater as people milled about, expressing shock it landed only feet from homes and only inches from passing vehicles. Thick black smoke engulfed the crash site.
It was unclear if the crash caused any damage to homes.

The crash occurred near Military Trail and 10th Avenue North. The Palm Beach county sheriff’s office closed roads in both directions and urged motorists to avoid the area. Firefighters and other emergency personnel rushed to the scene.
A woman working nearby said electricity in the area had been out for approximately two hours following the crash.
The circumstances of the crash remained under investigation.

飞机从奥斯汀-博格斯多姆国际机场起飞，前往巴哈马时坠毁
美国交通部长肖恩·达菲 (Sean Duffy) 表示，周日，一架商务飞机在佛罗里达州一个社区坠毁，机上九人全部遇难。这架飞机爆发出一个巨大的火球，似乎只是错过了一些房屋，然后在繁忙的道路附近坠毁。
周日，达菲在 X 上发布消息称，里尔 60 飞机于中午 12 点 50 分在棕榈滩县坠毁，并称这是一场“可怕的悲剧”。他说，美国联邦航空管理局正在派出一个团队来支持国家运输安全委员会对事故原因的调查。
据美国联邦航空管理局称，这架飞机已从德克萨斯州奥斯汀-博格斯多姆国际机场起飞，飞往巴哈马。当局没有立即说明飞机坠落的原因以及机上人员是谁。
机场发言人吉姆·雷诺兹表示，这是一架私人飞机。他无法立即提供有关飞机上人员的详细信息。
他说该航班的尾号是N722BD。
车内人员拍摄的视频捕捉到了飞机从天上坠落、然后撞到道路附近并爆炸的可怕时刻。火山口周围的大块人行道周围火焰闪烁，人们走来走去，表达了对它降落在距离房屋仅几英尺、距离过往车辆仅几英寸的震惊。浓浓的黑烟吞没了坠机现场。
目前尚不清楚事故是否对房屋造成任何损坏。
事故发生在军事步道和第十大道北附近。棕榈滩县治安官办公室关闭了两个方向的道路，并敦促驾车者避开该地区。消防队员和其他急救人员赶到现场。

title_en: Trump administration's social media posts ahead of elections criticized for being inflammatory
title_zh: 特朗普政府在选举前的社交媒体帖子被批评具有煽动性
summary: The Trump administration’s online accounts have circulated images of a pumpkin carved with a sombrero design and a fake Halloween-themed background around a Black man apparently accused of food assistance fraud
summary_zh: 特朗普政府的在线账户流传了雕刻有宽边帽设计的南瓜和假万圣节主题背景的图片。
body_en: Trump administration's social media posts ahead of elections criticized for being inflammatory

The Trump administration’s online accounts have circulated images of a pumpkin carved with a sombrero design and a fake Halloween-themed background around a Black man apparently accused of food assistance fraud

The Trump administration’s online accounts are circulating images of a pumpkin carved with a sombrero design and a fake Halloween-themed background around a Black man apparently accused of food assistance fraud, in social media posts slammed by critics as inflammatory rhetoric.

Only days before the midterm elections, the posts coincide with the government’s sweeping campaign to show its aggressive immigration enforcement , and highlight efforts to crack down on fraud to save taxpayers money when rising healthcare costs and other economic stressors have made affordability a top voter concern.

Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins posted Saturday on the social platform X a photo of the Black man standing in front of stacks of what appear to be U.S. currency with the headline, SNAP FRAUDSTER, an apparent reference to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, formerly known as food stamps.
He is holding aloft what appears to be a bill set aflame.
“Some costumes come with a price tag. This one comes with a prison sentence,” it says to the backdrop of fake Spirit Halloween costume packaging.
Another photo posted by the White House on X on Thursday showed a pumpkin with the shape of a sombrero carved across it and the words “Spooky szn is here.”

The post by Rollins, who was nominated by Trump to serve as the U.S. Secretary of Agriculture in November 2024, appears to be taken from an Instagram post from September 2025 by an account under the name Shawty Dred.

Earlier this month, Mercedes Reshard New, identified by the Justice Department as a social media personality also known as “Shawty Dred,” was arrested on federal charges for fraudulently obtaining more than $4 million in Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program benefits in Georgia.
It’s not the first time the White House has been accused of posting inflammatory images on official government social media accounts.

Just over a year ago during the government shutdown, the White House revived a deepfake video posted by Trump of House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries in a fake mustache and sombrero to accuse the Democrats of acting on behalf of illegal immigrants instead of U.S. citizens. Jeffries described the meme as bigoted. They played it on repeat in the White House briefing room, though Vice President JD Vance promised that the “sombrero memes will stop” when Democrats agreed to end the shutdown.
The NAACP did not respond to an email seeking comment, nor did the White House or Rollins.

1 dead, 6 injured in 'targeted' shooting at California Halloween store
2 college students found dead after going missing while hiking, police say

The Trump administration in recent weeks has ratcheted up its anti-immigrant rhetoric and accusations of fraud, including against U.S. Rep. Ilhan Omar whose Washington, D.C., home was searched by federal agents earlier this month. Federal authorities are investigating potential fraud in her family’s immigration paperwork. Omar, who was born in Somalia, is a naturalized U.S. citizen.

It also has taken a series of punitive steps linked to allegations of fraud in mostly Democratic-led states , including California and Minnesota whose governors accused the federal government of targeting their states for political reasons.

Federal prosecutors said in a news release Oct. 21 that the influencer, New, controlled more than 350 fraudulent SNAP accounts under stolen identities between January 2020 and July 2026. He allegedly applied for his company, Shawty Dred LLC, to become an authorized SNAP retailer and used EBT debit cards to extract about $4 million from the accounts.

New’s Instagram account, which has more than two million followers, has flaunted his extravagant lifestyle, federal prosecutors said. Posts depict him flying on private jets, posing with Rolls-Royce vehicles in front of his “super mansion,” and handling massive stacks of cash.
body_zh: 特朗普政府在选举前的社交媒体帖子被批评具有煽动性
特朗普政府的在线账户流传了一个雕刻有宽边帽设计的南瓜和一个假万圣节主题背景的图像，围绕着一名显然被指控食品援助欺诈的黑人
特朗普政府的网络账户在社交媒体帖子中传播了雕刻有宽边帽设计的南瓜和假万圣节主题背景围绕一名显然被指控食品援助欺诈的黑人的图片，这些图片被批评者抨击为煽动性言论。
就在中期选举前几天，这些帖子恰逢政府开展大规模宣传活动，以展示其积极的移民执法，并强调在医疗费用上涨和其他经济压力因素使负担能力成为选民最关心的问题之际，打击欺诈行为以节省纳税人的钱。
农业部长布鲁克·罗林斯周六在社交平台 X 上发布了一张黑人男子站在一堆看似美元的货币前的照片，标题为“SNAP FRAUDSTER”，显然是指补充营养援助计划（以前称为食品券）。
他高举着一张似乎已着火的钞票。
“有些服装带有价格标签。这款服装则需被判入狱，”它在假冒的精神万圣节服装包装的背景下说道。
周四，白宫在 X 上发布的另一张照片显示，一个南瓜上刻着宽边帽的形状，上面写着“Spooky szn is here”。
罗林斯于 2024 年 11 月被特朗普提名担任美国农业部长，他的帖子似乎取自 Shawty Dred 帐户于 2025 年 9 月发布的 Instagram 帖子。
本月早些时候，梅塞德斯·雷沙德·纽（Mercedes Reshard New）被司法部认定为社交媒体名人，也被称为“Shawty Dred”，因联邦指控在佐治亚州以欺诈手段获取超过 400 万美元的补充营养援助计划福利而被捕。
这并不是白宫第一次被指控在政府官方社交媒体账户上发布煽动性图片。
就在一年多前，政府关门期间，白宫重新播放了特朗普发布的一段深度假视频，视频中众议院民主党领袖哈基姆·杰弗里斯戴着假胡子和宽边帽，指责民主党代表非法移民而不是美国公民行事。杰弗里斯形容这个模因是偏执的。他们在白宫简报室重复播放了这段视频，尽管副总统 JD 万斯承诺，当民主党同意结束政府关门时，“宽边帽模因将会停止”。
全国有色人种协进会没有回复寻求置评的电子邮件，白宫或罗林斯也没有回复。

最近几周，特朗普政府加大了反移民言论和欺诈指控，其中包括针对美国众议员伊尔汗·奥马尔(Ilhan Omar)的欺诈指控，本月早些时候，联邦特工搜查了他在华盛顿特区的家。联邦当局正在调查她家人的移民文件中潜在的欺诈行为。奥马尔出生于索马里，已入籍美国公民。
它还针对大多数民主党领导的州的欺诈指控采取了一系列惩罚措施，其中包括加利福尼亚州和明尼苏达州，这两个州的州长指责联邦政府出于政治原因针对其州。
联邦检察官在 10 月 21 日的新闻稿中表示，网红 New 在 2020 年 1 月至 2026 年 7 月期间以被盗身份控制了 350 多个欺诈性 SNAP 账户。据称，他向自己的公司 Shawty Dred LLC 申请成为 SNAP 授权零售商，并使用 EBT 借记卡从账户中提取了约 400 万美元。
联邦检察官称，纽的 Instagram 账户拥有超过 200 万粉丝，该账户一直在炫耀他奢华的生活方式。帖子描述了他乘坐私人飞机、在他的“超级豪宅”前与劳斯莱斯汽车合影、处理大量现金。
