summary_zh: 周二中期选举之后，OpenAI 将发起一项政策和公关闪电战，试图与新华盛顿保持同步，包括重新命名的努力
body_en: Right after Tuesday's midterms, OpenAI will unleash a policy and PR blitz to try to get in sync with the new Washington, including an effort to rebrand data centers as "AI compute campuses."

Why it matters: After two years of a friendly White House, AI companies will face a harsher Washington after Tuesday, when Democrats will likely win the House. OpenAI also aims to help frame the AI debate for the big field of 2028 presidential contenders that'll start forming on Wednesday.

"You can try to chase the moment, or seek to inform the moment via the power of ideas," OpenAI chief global affairs officer Chris Lehane tells us, calling Tuesday an "electoral portal from one era to the next."
Since August, Lehane and his team have been stockpiling policy proposals, some new and some repackaged, to drive urgency and steer the AI debate.

It'll all start during the lame-duck session of Congress — the awkward but often consequential weeks between the election and the swearing-in of new members and senators on Jan. 3. This year's lame duck opens Nov. 9.

The big picture: Other tech companies are also positioning themselves for a potential blue wave. Meta is taking steps to strengthen its ties with Democrats, Axios' Sara Fischer scooped Saturday . Other big AI and tech players can be expected to do the same.
Tech titans who enjoy close relationships with President Trump will be top targets for Democrats, who are eager to ramp up scrutiny and regulatory pressure on the industry.
OpenAI's plans, being revealed here for the first time, all involve control — trying to send the message that AI is being built for people, not to displace people. The proposals include

Speed limits: Building on earlier proposals , OpenAI plans to unveil new ideas for mandatory safeguards for the most powerful AI systems — speed limits for AI that will allow humans to keep their hands on the wheel. This'll include a more aggressive congressional drive. "You're going to see us talk more and more about the concept of speed limits," Lehane said. "Our belief is people should always remain in control of this technology. AI should be built by and for people, and people should have more control over how the technology shapes their lives and communities."

Data centers: OpenAI hopes to stem the nationwide, bipartisan backlash by offering new community compacts and commitments to smooth the way for future data centers. In addition, the company will try to set a new industry standard by proposing state legislation that gives people a meaningful say in how projects are built and what benefits they receive. In an intentionally provocative rebranding effort, OpenAI will argue that the infrastructure it's building, in contrast to legacy data centers, should be called "AI compute campuses" that can economically transform host communities. OpenAI points to its role in developing a huge data center project that promises to bring thousands of jobs to Pike County in Ohio's Appalachian region. "We think the conversation is good and healthy," Lehane said. "It's democracy in action. Communities should hold companies responsible and accountable so they really and truly get a transformative benefit from these projects."

Economic opportunity: OpenAI is developing ideas to help more people see AI as empowering for their daily lives and on the job, including supporting workers through disruption, widening access to education and training, and making it easier to start and grow a business.
International cooperation: OpenAI will push for the U.S. to shape global standards with AI built on democratic values.
Between the lines: OpenAI is trying to stake out a human-centered "third path" in a debate that often defaults to an artificial binary of doomers vs. accelerationists.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, speaking to the UN Security Council in September, called for an AI approach that leads to a "new Renaissance of creativity and discovery."

What we're watching: OpenAI's overtures are aimed partly at 2028 presidential hopefuls, who'll be increasingly vocal about their plans starting Wednesday. "AI is going to be the issue in 2028," Lehane said, calling the midterms a "bit of a movie trailer for what you're going to see in 2028."

"I don't think it's going to be good enough just to say 'AI bad,'" Lehane added. "The public gets that this is a much more complex, nuanced conversation. They're going to be looking for whoever their FDR or Lincoln is who's actually going to want to try to lead them through this journey."

Lehane said candidates should ask: "How do we start to think about trust? How do we think about the incredible anxiety that exists in modernity? How do we think about the fact that people are profoundly unhappy with where their social contract is, where the American dream is?"

The bottom line: The plans for the coming months are just the beginning of OpenAI's effort to inject more urgency in Washington and push the industry on frontier safety. Remember: Every day, AI models get more powerful — and tougher to corral.

"Our policy priorities — and urgency, especially on frontier safety — are about meeting the moment in response to the rapidly advancing capabilities," Lehane said. "And we expect that to continue as a new Congress ramps up."
Disclosure: Axios has a content licensing and technology agreement with OpenAI, emphasizing expansion of local news coverage.
body_zh: 周二中期选举之后，OpenAI 将推出一项政策和公关闪电战，试图与新华盛顿保持同步，包括将数据中心重新命名为“人工智能计算园区”。
为什么重要：在白宫友好地待了两年之后，周二之后，人工智能公司将面临更加严厉的华盛顿，届时民主党可能会赢得众议院。 OpenAI 还旨在帮助构建将于周三开始形成的 2028 年总统竞选人的人工智能辩论。
OpenAI 首席全球事务官 Chris Lehane 告诉我们：“你可以尝试追逐这一时刻，或者寻求通过思想的力量来传达这一时刻。”他称周二为“从一个时代到下一个时代的选举门户”。
自 8 月以来，Lehane 和他的团队一直在储备政策提案，其中一些是新的，一些是重新包装的，以提高紧迫性并引导人工智能辩论。
这一切都将从国会的“跛脚鸭”会议开始——从选举到 1 月 3 日新议员和参议员宣誓就职之间的尴尬但往往重要的几周。今年的“跛脚鸭”会议将于 11 月 9 日开幕。
总体情况：其他科技公司也在为潜在的蓝色浪潮做好准备。 Axios 的 Sara Fischer 周六报道称，Meta 正在采取措施加强与民主党的联系。预计其他大型人工智能和科技公司也会采取同样的做法。
与特朗普总统关系密切的科技巨头将成为民主党的首要目标，他们渴望加大对该行业的审查和监管压力。
OpenAI 的计划首次在这里披露，全部都涉及控制——试图传达这样的信息：人工智能是为人类而构建，而不是取代人类。这些建议包括
速度限制：在早期提案的基础上，OpenAI 计划推出新的想法，为最强大的人工智能系统提供强制保护——人工智能的速度限制，让人类能够把手放在方向盘上。这将包括更积极的国会推动。 “你会看到我们越来越多地谈论速度限制的概念，”勒哈恩说。 “我们的信念是，人们应该始终保持对这项技术的控制。人工智能应该由人们构建并为人们服务，人们应该更好地控制技术如何塑造他们的生活和社区。”

数据中心：OpenAI 希望通过提供新的社区契约和承诺来遏制全国范围内两党的强烈反对，为未来的数据中心铺平道路。此外，该公司将尝试通过提出州立法来制定新的行业标准，让人们在项目如何建设以及他们获得什么利益方面拥有有意义的发言权。在一次有意挑衅性的品牌重塑工作中，OpenAI 将辩称，与传统数据中心相比，它正在构建的基础设施应该被称为“AI 计算园区”，可以在经济上改变所在社区。 OpenAI 指出了其在开发一个大型数据中心项目中的作用，该项目有望为俄亥俄州阿巴拉契亚地区的派克县带来数千个就业机会。 “我们认为这次对话是良好且健康的，”勒哈恩说。 “这是行动中的民主。社区应该让公司承担起责任和责任，这样他们才能真正从这些项目中获得变革性的好处。”
经济机遇：OpenAI 正在开发创意，帮助更多人将人工智能视为日常生活和工作的助力，包括支持员工应对颠覆、扩大教育和培训机会，以及让创业和发展业务变得更容易。
国际合作：OpenAI 将推动美国制定基于民主价值观的人工智能全球标准。
言外之意是：OpenAI 正试图在一场辩论中指出一条以人为本的“第三条道路”，这场辩论通常默认为末日论者与加速论者的人为二元论。
OpenAI 首席执行官萨姆·奥尔特曼 (Sam Altman) 9 月份在联合国安理会发表讲话，呼吁采用人工智能方法来引领“创造力和发现的新复兴”。
我们正在关注的内容：OpenAI 的提议部分针对 2028 年总统候选人，从周三开始，他们将越来越多地公开表达自己的计划。 Lehane 表示：“人工智能将成为 2028 年的问题。”他将中期选举称为“你将在 2028 年看到的电影预告片”。
“我认为仅仅说‘人工智能不好’还不够好，”勒哈恩补充道。 “公众知道这是一个更加复杂、细致的对话。他们将寻找真正愿意带领他们完成这一旅程的罗斯福或林肯。”
勒哈恩说，候选人应该问：“我们如何开始考虑信任？我们如何考虑现代社会中存在的令人难以置信的焦虑？我们如何考虑人们对自己的社会契约和美国梦深感不满的事实？”
底线：未来几个月的计划只是 OpenAI 努力的开始，该计划旨在向华盛顿注入更多紧迫感，并推动该行业实现边境安全。请记住：人工智能模型每天都变得更强大，也更难控制。
勒哈恩说：“我们的政策优先事项和紧迫性，特别是在边境安全方面，是为了应对快速发展的能力。” “我们预计，随着新一届国会的成立，这种情况将继续下去。”
披露：Axios 与 OpenAI 签订了内容许可和技术协议，强调扩大本地新闻报道。

title_en: Trump's election probes find an opening in Georgia
title_zh: 特朗普的选举调查在佐治亚州找到了漏洞
summary: On the eve of midterms, President Trump is facing setbacks left and right in his push to investigate alleged election fraud . But in Georgia, he has an opening. Why it matters: Six years ago, Georgia was at the epicenter of Trump's efforts to overturn the 2020
summary_zh: 中期选举前夕，特朗普总统在推动调查涉嫌选举舞弊的行动中面临着左右挫折。但在佐治亚州，他有一个
body_en: On the eve of midterms, President Trump is facing setbacks left and right in his push to investigate alleged election fraud . But in Georgia, he has an opening.

Why it matters: Six years ago, Georgia was at the epicenter of Trump's efforts to overturn the 2020 presidential election. Now the state's own election board has invited his administration to investigate its voting system.

Georgia features two high-stakes statewide campaigns: Sen. Jon Ossoff (D) against Rep. Mike Collins (R) for Senate, and former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms (D) against businessman Rick Jackson (R) for governor.

The big picture: The Justice Department disclosed in court on Friday that the administration has sent letters to officials in California, Washington, Pennsylvania, New Jersey and Nevada, asking some states to segregate mail-in ballots from suspected noncitizen voters.
A federal judge on Friday issued an emergency order that blocks federal officials from threatening to charge election officials who count ballots from voters the DOJ claims are ineligible.
In October, a federal judge restricted the Department of Homeland Security's investigations into suspected noncitizen voters.

But Georgia is different . "We've managed with duct tape and bubble gum to be able to bootstrap our way through one last round, but that's not a way of running elections," a Georgia election official told Axios.
Georgia's State Election Board asked the Justice and Homeland Security departments to review and potentially investigate the state's voting system and handling of election data.
The Sept. 30 letter cited outdated software, threats to ballot secrecy and QR-code ballots it says may violate the Help America Vote Act.

A DOJ spokesperson said in response to the letter: "We take seriously allegations that election officials have failed to adequately maintain election equipment and otherwise comply with federal law. We are evaluating the request and will investigate and, if appropriate, bring an enforcement action consistent with federal law."

The other side: Georgia State Election Board Chair John Fevrier , appointed by Gov. Brian Kemp (R), opposed the letter and told Axios that a majority of the board now believes it "far exceeded what was in the resolution."
Michon Lindstrom, senior director of communications for Georgia's secretary of state, said: "It's unfortunate that the state election board sought to inject chaos in the 11th hour of the election."
In 2020, Georgia Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger rebuffed Trump's efforts to overturn Georgia's presidential election results.
Friction point: Georgia has spent years debating how to address vulnerabilities in its voting system.

The secretary of state's office said Georgia's machines haven't been updated since they were purchased in 2019. The state said it's starting a procurement process for new machines for the next election cycle.

The state's legislature passed a law in 2024 to move away from a QR-code ballot system to hand-marked paper ballots. This transition was supposed to be implemented by this July, but lawmakers passed a deadline extension.
A software glitch on the state's tabulators that could impact ballot secrecy has been known to the state since 2022. But an available fix hasn't been installed.

Between the lines: "There are no clean hands in this," the Georgia election official told Axios. "The secretary of state could have fought harder for the funding... [The] legislature could have funded it when the secretary of state asked for it. But ... they all have pissed each other off so much."

In 2025, Raffensperger urged lawmakers to reconsider a $47 million voting-machine upgrade, proposing a software update costing less than $15 million or delaying any purchases until the existing contract expired.
In 2026, Raffensperger told legislators that there wasn't money for any election upgrades. No upgrades were funded.
body_zh: 中期选举前夕，特朗普总统在推动调查涉嫌选举舞弊的行动中面临着左右挫折。但在佐治亚州，他有一个空缺。
重要性：六年前，佐治亚州是特朗普推翻 2020 年总统选举努力的中心。现在，该州自己的选举委员会已邀请他的政府调查其投票系统。
佐治亚州有两场全州范围内的高风险竞选活动：参议员乔恩·奥索夫（民主党）与众议员迈克·柯林斯（右）竞选参议员，前亚特兰大市长凯莎·兰斯·博顿斯（民主党）对阵商人里克·杰克逊（右）竞选州长。
大局：司法部周五在法庭上透露，政府已致函加利福尼亚州、华盛顿州、宾夕法尼亚州、新泽西州和内华达州的官员，要求一些州将邮寄选票与疑似非公民选民分开。
周五，一名联邦法官发布了一项紧急命令，禁止联邦官员威胁指控负责计票的选举官员，而司法部声称这些选民不具备资格。
十月，一名联邦法官限制国土安全部对可疑的非公民选民进行调查。
但格鲁吉亚不同。佐治亚州一名选举官员告诉 Axios：“我们已经用胶带和泡泡糖成功地完成了最后一轮选举，但这不是选举的一种方式。”
佐治亚州选举委员会要求司法和国土安全部门审查并可能调查该州的投票系统和选举数据的处理。
9 月 30 日的信函提到了过时的软件、对选票保密的威胁以及二维码选票，称这可能违反《帮助美国投票法》。
司法部发言人在回复这封信时表示：“我们严肃对待有关选举官员未能充分维护选举设备和遵守联邦法律的指控。我们正在评估这一请求，并将进行调查，并在适当的情况下采取符合联邦法律的执法行动。”
另一方：由州长布莱恩·坎普（R）任命的佐治亚州选举委员会主席约翰·费夫里尔（John Fevrier）反对这封信，并告诉 Axios，委员会的大多数成员现在认为这“远远超出了决议中的内容”。
佐治亚州国务卿高级通讯主任米洪·林德斯特罗姆 (Michon Lindstrom) 表示：“不幸的是，州选举委员会试图在选举进行的第 11 个小时内制造混乱。”
2020年，佐治亚州国务卿布拉德·拉芬斯佩格断然拒绝了特朗普推翻佐治亚州总统选举结果的努力。
摩擦点：佐治亚州多年来一直在争论如何解决其投票系统中的漏洞。
国务卿办公室表示，佐治亚州的机器自 2019 年购买以来就没有更新过。该州表示正在启动下一个选举周期新机器的采购流程。
该州立法机构于 2024 年通过了一项法律，从二维码投票系统转向手写纸质选票。这一过渡原定于今年 7 月实施，但立法者通过了期限延长。
自 2022 年以来，该州就已经知道该州制表机上存在一个可能影响选票保密的软件故障。但尚未安装可用的修复程序。
言外之意是：“这件事上没有干净的手，”佐治亚州选举官员告诉 Axios。 “国务卿本可以更加努力地争取资金……当国务卿提出要求时，立法机关本可以提供资金。但是……他们都让彼此非常生气。”
2025 年，拉芬斯伯格敦促立法者重新考虑耗资 4700 万美元的投票机升级，提议进行成本低于 1500 万美元的软件更新，或者推迟任何采购，直到现有合同到期。
2026 年，拉芬斯伯格告诉立法者，没有资金用于任何选举升级。没有资助升级。

title_en: Stevens endorses Rogers amid rift with El-Sayed
title_zh: 史蒂文斯在与埃尔赛义德不和的情况下支持罗杰斯
summary: Haley Stevens, who had the support of the Senate Democrats' campaign arm in the primary, had previously said she was supporting the Democratic ticket.
summary_zh: 海莉·史蒂文斯(Haley Stevens)在初选中得到了参议院民主党竞选部门的支持，此前她曾表示支持民主党。
body_en: Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens endorsed Michigan GOP Senate candidate Mike Rogers on Sunday amid a rift with Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed that has come front and center in the final sprint to Election Day.

"Our Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, Abdul, said that I was no longer welcome in his campaign and that I should stay away, and he's right," Stevens said in a video posted on social media Sunday. "And that's why I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the United States Senate today."
Stevens appeared alongside Rogers at a Detroit church on Sunday.

Stevens, who narrowly lost to El-Sayed in Michigan's Democratic primary in August, where she was heavily supported by the Senate Democrats' campaign arm, called on El-Sayed last week to condemn an outside group's ad linking U.S. military aid to Israel to rising grocery prices, which she characterized as antisemitic. El-Sayed accused Stevens of "relitigating a primary that ended three months ago," although he has also clarified that the ad "was not made by me" and said he disagrees with its contents.

El-Sayed pushed to return the attention to the issues facing Michigan voters as he takes on the GOP candidate, Rogers. But Rogers praised Stevens on Friday for calling on El-Sayed to denounce the ad, and for expressing concerns raised by Michigan Jewish voters.

"Representative Haley Stevens is a courageous leader who deserves the respect of every Michigan voter," Rogers said in a post on X. "She has conducted herself with nothing but class since the Democratic primary, a primary where a majority of voters did not vote for her party's nominee."
Speaking to reporters after he appeared with Stevens at the Detroit church Sunday, Rogers said he was honored to receive her support.
"This is more a statement about standing together against hate and the future of this state and this country than it is anything else," Rogers said.

Rogers said he got the call Sunday morning from Stevens, and the two decided to appear together at the church. He said he and Stevens talked about what was better for the future of the state. And he noted that Stevens reminded him at the end of their call that she remains a Democrat.
Responding to the endorsement on Sunday, El-Sayed said, "I actually don't think about Haley Stevens."
"This is a state of 10 million people who deserve a lot better from their government. I'm a lot more focused on the 9,999,998 that are not the ones who are talking about."
Stevens said she's "not trying to harm" the Democratic Party with the move, insisting that she isn't "turning her back on Democrats."
"It is this one vote," she said. "And I will tell you why: Because when you see hate, when you see us standing with Hasan Piker, and repeated hate, it's not acceptable."
"That's it. It's my personal and private decision," Stevens said. "It's a Michigan moment, and everyone is entitled to their opinion."
Stevens said she "meant it" when she previously endorsed El-Sayed. But she added, "He chose to close his campaign by saying I wasn't welcome."

The appearance with Rogers came after Stevens had been expected to appear with El-Sayed at a unity event Sunday alongside Rep. Jim Clyburn of South Carolina. But El-Sayed said Saturday, "I would rather not distract from the key issues of this campaign."
Stevens' fiancé, Jason Turkish, said last week that he is voting for Rogers.
Democrats stunned by reversal, Trump praises Stevens
After Stevens endorsed Rogers, top Democrats expressed their continued support for El-Sayed's candidacy, including Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer.

"Senate Democrats are united in our support for Abdul El-Sayed, because we know he will fight for the economic interests of working families in Michigan, unlike Mike Rogers, who is a tool of Donald Trump and billionaire donors," Schumer said in a statement.
body_zh: 民主党众议员海莉·史蒂文斯周日支持密歇根州共和党参议院候选人迈克·罗杰斯，因为他与民主党参议院候选人阿卜杜勒·赛义德之间存在分歧，这一分歧在选举日的最后冲刺中成为焦点。
史蒂文斯周日在社交媒体上发布的视频中说：“我们的美国参议院民主党候选人阿卜杜勒说，我不再欢迎他参加他的竞选活动，我应该离开，他是对的。” “这就是为什么我今天支持迈克·罗杰斯竞选美国参议院。”
周日，史蒂文斯与罗杰斯一起出现在底特律的一座教堂。
史蒂文斯在八月份的密歇根州民主党初选中以微弱优势输给了埃尔赛义德，在那里她得到了参议院民主党竞选部门的大力支持。史蒂文斯上周呼吁埃尔赛义德谴责一个外部团体的广告，该广告将美国对以色列的军事援助与不断上涨的杂货价格联系起来，她将其视为反犹太主义。埃尔-赛义德指责史蒂文斯“对三个月前结束的初选重新提起诉讼”，尽管他也澄清该广告“不是我制作的”，并表示他不同意其内容。
埃尔-赛义德在与共和党候选人罗杰斯较量时，力图让人们重新关注密歇根州选民面临的问题。但罗杰斯周五赞扬史蒂文斯呼吁埃尔赛义德谴责这则广告，并表达了密歇根犹太选民提出的担忧。
罗杰斯在 X 上的一篇帖子中表示：“海莉·史蒂文斯代表是一位勇敢的领导人，值得每一位密歇根州选民的尊重。自民主党初选以来，她一直表现得很优雅，在这次初选中，大多数选民没有投票给她所在政党的提名人。”
罗杰斯周日与史蒂文斯一起出现在底特律教堂后对记者说，他很荣幸得到她的支持。
罗杰斯说：“这更多的是关于团结起来反对仇恨以及这个州和这个国家的未来的声明，而不是其他任何东西。”
罗杰斯说，他周日早上接到了史蒂文斯的电话，两人决定一起出现在教堂。他说他和史蒂文斯讨论了什么对国家的未来更好。他指出，史蒂文斯在通话结束时提醒他，她仍然是民主党人。
周日，埃尔-赛义德在回应这一支持时表示：“我实际上并没有想到海莉·史蒂文斯。”
“这是一个由 1000 万人组成的国家，他们应该从政府那里得到更好的待遇。我更关注的是 9,999,998 个人，他们不是我们正在谈论的人。”
史蒂文斯表示，她的举动“并不是想伤害”民主党，并坚称她并没有“背弃民主党”。
“就这一票，”她说。 “我会告诉你原因：因为当你看到仇恨，当你看到我们与哈桑·派克站在一起，并重复仇恨，这是不可接受的。”
“就是这样。这是我个人的私人决定，”史蒂文斯说。 “这是密歇根时刻，每个人都有权发表自己的意见。”
史蒂文斯表示，她之前支持埃尔赛义德时是“认真的”。但她补充道，“他选择以说我不受欢迎来结束他的竞选活动。”
史蒂文斯预计将与罗杰斯一起出现在周日与南卡罗来纳州众议员吉姆·克莱伯恩一起参加的统一活动中。但埃尔-赛义德周六表示，“我不想分散对这次竞选的关键问题的注意力。”
史蒂文斯的未婚夫杰森·土耳其上周表示，他将投票给罗杰斯。
民主党人对逆转感到震惊，特朗普称赞史蒂文斯
史蒂文斯支持罗杰斯后，民主党高层表示继续支持埃尔赛义德的候选资格，其中包括参议院少数党领袖查克·舒默。
舒默在一份声明中表示：“参议院民主党人团结一致支持阿卜杜勒·赛义德，因为我们知道他将为密歇根州工薪家庭的经济利益而奋斗，这与唐纳德·特朗普和亿万富翁捐助者的工具迈克·罗杰斯不同。”

title_en: It's ACA open enrollment time. Here are the changes for health insurance shoppers
title_zh: 现在是 ACA 开放报名时间。以下是健康保险购买者的变化
summary: The ACA health insurance marketplaces — find yours at HealthCare.gov — open Nov. 1 for 2027 coverage. Getting an early start may be especially important this year.
summary_zh: ACA 健康保险市场（请在 HealthCare.gov 上找到您的市场）将于 11 月 1 日开放，提供 2027 年承保范围。尽早开始可能尤其重要
body_en: It's ACA open enrollment time. Here are the changes for health insurance shoppers

Christine Meehan, a hair stylist in Upper Chichester, Pa., has purchased health insurance through Pennie , the ACA marketplace for Pennsylvania. She's pictured here in October 2025. ACA open enrollment runs from Nov. 1 through Jan. 15 in most states. Tassanee Vejpongsa/AP hide caption

Consumers who buy Affordable Care Act health insurance are going to see changes both big and small as open enrollment for 2027 coverage kicks off. These include premium increases, possible additional identity checks, potential delays in working with a broker, and new limits on which immigrants can get subsidies.
Open enrollment starts Nov. 1 in most states . Idaho, Connecticut, and Massachusetts started earlier, and some states have been allowing "window shopping" to check premium rates.

A continued decline in overall enrollment is expected, mainly because of the expiration of enhanced subsidies at the end of 2025. Policy experts say the end of those subsidies led millions to drop or lose coverage through the first few months of this year.
After booting 760K off ACA health plans, the Trump administration adds some people back

But the Trump administration sees victory in the falling enrollment, crediting its various efforts to reduce fraud, including the August cancellation of policies covering 760,000 enrollees suspected to be improperly signed up. A small number of those enrollees have regained coverage .

One of the biggest changes for people shopping for their 2027 coverage will be increased scrutiny of both consumers and agents. The requirements are aimed at thwarting fraud or improper enrollments. For consumers, it could slow the enrollment process.

The new rules , outlined by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, affect only consumers using agents or brokers to help them enroll through the federal marketplace, which serves 29 states. They do not apply to state-based exchanges, which have their own rules and have in most cases been more successful at preventing fraudulent sign-ups.

For starters, all consumers using an agent in the federal marketplace will need to get a one-time confirmation code or link to authorize a specific agent to enroll them or make changes on their behalf. It will be sent to consumers by text message, email, or an automated phone call from one of the private enrollment platforms used by their agent. Returning consumers who have incorrect or outdated contact information will first need to call the federal marketplace themselves or submit an application online to update it.

Additionally, consumers and policyholders deemed "high-risk" must verify their own identity before authorizing an agent. CMS defines as "high-risk" first-time applicants or those with existing coverage whose applications involve a change of state, as well as consumers working with a new or different agent or with a monthly premium payment of $30 or less.

Joshua Brooker, who oversees an insurance agency in Pennsylvania, said CMS appears to have selected people in those groups for greater scrutiny because "someone who is moving to a new state or switching brokers — that could be a broker trying to impersonate a consumer."

The $30-a-month cutoff may be tied to concerns that plans with no or low monthly premiums are easier for bad agents to target for unauthorized enrollments because the policyholder may never get a bill. Some rogue agents even pay the low monthly amount themselves and still make a profit from the commission, Brooker said.
The broad nature of the new rules, though, has Brooker concerned "that up to 1 in 5 consumers is going to have to do extra identity proofing" and may just give up and not get insured.

Consumers designated high-risk must prove their identity through a CMS-approved third party such as credit company Experian, which generally asks questions only the consumer should be able to answer. People who fail this test may be asked to call Experian's help desk or submit their applications themselves by creating a healthcare.gov account, which requires them to upload identification such as a driver's license, a passport, immigration papers, or another form of ID .

"Some people may have trouble not because they're not real, but because they don't have a credit file, or have moved, or have changed names," said Stacey Pogue , a senior research fellow at the Center on Health Insurance Reforms at Georgetown University.
She said the changes might "be an appropriate response by CMS that targets fraudulent enrollments but might also create extra hurdles."

CMS in September issued a rule that places a moratorium on brokers new to offering ACA coverage. Agents not registered with the federal marketplace in 2026 will not be allowed to assist with enrollments for 2027 until February at the earliest, past the end of open enrollment season.

CMS said it took this step because a disproportionate number of "significant compliance concerns" in 2026 came from newly registered agents or brokers. Additionally, the agency has kicked out "hundreds of non-compliant agents and brokers" this year.
5 million have dropped ACA insurance after Trump and the GOP let prices skyrocket
body_zh: 现在是 ACA 开放报名时间。以下是健康保险购买者的变化
Christine Meehan 是宾夕法尼亚州上奇切斯特的一名发型师，她通过宾夕法尼亚州 ACA 市场 Pennie 购买了健康保险。照片摄于 2025 年 10 月。在大多数州，ACA 开放注册时间为 11 月 1 日至 1 月 15 日。 Tassanee Vejpongsa/美联社隐藏标题栏
随着 2027 年保险范围的公开投保开始，购买《平价医疗法案》健康保险的消费者将看到大大小小的变化。其中包括保费增加、可能的额外身份检查、与经纪人合作的潜在延迟以及移民获得补贴的新限制。
大多数州于 11 月 1 日开始开放招生。爱达荷州、康涅狄格州和马萨诸塞州起步较早，一些州已经允许“橱窗购物”来检查保费率。
预计总体入学率将持续下降，主要是因为增强补贴将于 2025 年底到期。政策专家表示，这些补贴的终止导致数百万人在今年头几个月减少或失去保险。
在将 76 万人从 ACA 健康计划中剔除后，特朗普政府又重新增加了一些人
但特朗普政府认为入学率下降取得了胜利，这归功于其为减少欺诈所做的各种努力，包括 8 月份取消了覆盖 76 万名涉嫌不当注册的参保者的保单。其中少数参保者已重新获得保险。
对于购买 2027 年保险的人们来说，最大的变化之一将是对消费者和代理商的审查更加严格。这些要求旨在阻止欺诈或不当注册。对于消费者来说，这可能会减慢注册过程。
医疗保险和医疗补助服务中心概述的新规则仅影响使用代理人或经纪人帮助他们通过联邦市场进行注册的消费者，该市场为 29 个州提供服务。它们不适用于基于州的交易所，这些交易所有自己的规则，并且在大多数情况下在防止欺诈性注册方面更加成功。
首先，所有在联邦市场使用代理的消费者都需要获得一次性确认码或链接，以授权特定代理为他们注册或代表他们进行更改。它将通过短信、电子邮件或自动电话从其代理人使用的私人注册平台之一发送给消费者。如果联系信息不正确或过时，返回的消费者首先需要亲自致电联邦市场或在线提交申请以更新信息。
此外，被视为“高风险”的消费者和投保人必须在授权代理人之前验证自己的身份。 CMS 将“高风险”首次申请人或现有承保范围内的申请人（其申请涉及状态变更）以及与新的或不同的代理人合作或每月保费支付 30 美元或以下的消费者定义为“高风险”。
宾夕法尼亚州一家保险机构的负责人约书亚·布鲁克 (Joshua Brooker) 表示，CMS 似乎选择了这些群体中的人员进行更严格的审查，因为“搬到新州或更换经纪人的人可能是试图冒充消费者的经纪人。”
每月 30 美元的截止额可能与担心无月保费或月保费较低的计划更容易被不良代理人针对未经授权的投保进行攻击，因为投保人可能永远不会收到账单。布鲁克说，一些流氓代理商甚至自己支付较低的每月金额，但仍然从佣金中获利。
然而，新规则的广泛性让布鲁克担心“多达五分之一的消费者将不得不进行额外的身份验证”，并且可能会放弃而无法获得保险。
被指定为高风险的消费者必须通过 CMS 批准的第三方（例如信贷公司 Experian）证明其身份，该公司通常会提出只有消费者能够回答的问题。未通过此测试的人可能会被要求致电 Experian 服务台或通过创建healthcare.gov 帐户自行提交申请，这要求他们上传身份证明，例如驾驶执照、护照、移民文件或其他形式的身份证件。
乔治城大学健康保险改革中心的高级研究员史黛西·波格说：“有些人可能遇到麻烦，不是因为他们不是真实的，而是因为他们没有信用档案，或者搬家了，或者改了名字。”
她表示，这些变化可能“是 CMS 针对欺诈注册的适当回应，但也可能会造成额外的障碍。”
CMS 在 9 月份发布了一项规则，暂停新提供 ACA 保险的经纪商。未在 2026 年在联邦市场注册的代理商最早要到 2 月（开放招生季结束后）才能协助 2027 年的招生。
CMS 表示，之所以采取这一措施，是因为 2026 年“重大合规问题”来自新注册代理商或经纪人的数量不成比例。此外，该机构今年还驱逐了“数百名不合规的代理人和经纪人”。

title_en: How Gen Z Republicans running for Congress are thinking about the future of the party
title_zh: 竞选国会议员的 Z 世代共和党人如何思考该党的未来
summary: On the eve of what may prove to be a tough election for the GOP, young conservatives vying to be part of the first class of Gen Z Republicans in Congress want a role shaping the party's next chapter.
summary_zh: 在共和党可能面临一场艰难选举的前夕，年轻的保守派人士竞相成为国会第一批 Z 世代共和党人的一员。
body_en: How Gen Z Republicans running for Congress are thinking about the future of the party

Joe Mitchell, seen at the Iowa State Fair on Aug. 14, 2026, is the GOP nominee in Iowa's 2nd congressional district. He is one of just a handful of Gen-Z Republicans on the ballot for the U.S. House this year. Scott Olson/Getty Images hide caption

In northeast Iowa, 29-year-old Joe Mitchell is vying to represent the state's second congressional district. It's a competitive race, one of just a handful considered to be a tossup , as voters sour on President Trump and Democrats see control of Congress as increasingly in reach.
Mitchell has the president's endorsement, and if he's successful, he would head to Washington D.C. next year as part of a new cohort: the first-ever class of Gen Z Republicans in Congress.

It wouldn't be a large class. Aside from Mitchell, just a handful of other Gen Z Republicans are in the running for House seats this fall. One is running in a reliably red district. The rest are longshots, vying for what's seen as safe blue seats.
While their numbers may be small, Mitchell says the idea of a new generation of leaders in Washington is something that voters have been responding to on the campaign trail.
"I think people are looking for hope, regardless of what party they're in," he said. "They want to see young people get involved, and I hear that everywhere we go."
Can I trust the polls? And other questions from listeners about the 2026 midterms

The former state senator and real estate developer says his platform can speak to Iowans on both sides of the aisle. He's calling for term limits in the House, with a maximum of six terms, as well as a ban on congressional stock trading. He says he has also rejected campaign donations from corporate PACs.

It's all part of an "anti-corruption platform," a focus he says is uniquely rooted in his generation, as Americans under 30 report high levels of concern for their economic wellbeing and distrust of institutions.
"I just think that young people — on both sides of the aisle or no party affiliates — are frustrated with the system," he said. "They're frustrated and they should be."

Currently, just one member of the House is part of Gen Z: 29-year-old Florida Democrat Maxwell Frost. However, two additional candidates are expected to win on Tuesday. Democratic socialist Melat Kiros , 29, is favored to win in Colorado's 1st district, a reliably blue seat. Republican Michael Alfonso, 26, is expected to carry Wisconsin's 7th district, a heavily Republican seat.

Alfonso, a political newcomer endorsed by Trump, is married to the daughter of Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, who previously held the seat from 2011 until 2019. If elected, he would be the first person born in the 2000s to serve in Congress.
In an interview with Wisconsin Public Radio earlier this month, Alfonso called his age his "greatest advantage."

Michael Alfonso, a candidate for U.S. House in Wisconsin's 7th congressional district, shakes hands with attendees during a campaign event on Aug. 4, 2026, in New Richmond, Wisc. Ellen Schmidt/AP hide caption
"I have the same values of everyone here in the 7th [district,]" said Alfonso. "Hard work, faith and family."

But running and winning as a candidate in their 20s remains a rarity in politics. With the oldest Gen Zers turning 30 next year, it's a generation that's only just starting to become eligible to serve in the House, which has an age minimum of 25.

Just 4% of congressional candidates nationwide this cycle were part of Gen Z, which was the least likely of any generation to make it past the primary, according to a report from Future Caucus , a nonpartisan organization supporting young people in elected office.
Plus, while running for Congress as a young person remains rare, doing so as a young Republican is even less common.

Future Caucus data reveals that a majority of Gen Z candidates who ran for Congress this year ran as Democrats, while under a third filed as Republicans. Another 16% did not associate with either party or selected a third party.
body_zh: 竞选国会议员的 Z 世代共和党人如何思考该党的未来
2026 年 8 月 14 日，乔·米切尔 (Joe Mitchell) 出现在爱荷华州博览会上，他是爱荷华州第二国会选区的共和党提名人。他是今年参加美国众议院选举的少数 Z 世代共和党人之一。斯科特·奥尔森/盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏
在爱荷华州东北部，29 岁的乔·米切尔正在竞选该州第二个国会选区的代表。这是一场竞争激烈的竞选，是为数不多的几场被认为是一场势均力敌的竞选之一，因为选民对特朗普总统感到不满，而民主党人则认为对国会的控制越来越近。
米切尔得到了总统的支持，如果他成功了，他将于明年作为新群体的一部分前往华盛顿特区：国会中第一批 Z 世代共和党人。
这不会是一个大班。除了米切尔之外，只有少数 Z 世代共和党人正在竞选今年秋天的众议院席位。其中一个正在可靠的红色区域运行。其余的人则希望渺茫，争夺被视为安全的蓝色席位。
米切尔说，虽然他们的人数可能很少，但华盛顿新一代领导人的想法是选民在竞选过程中一直在回应的想法。
“我认为人们都在寻找希望，无论他们属于哪个政党，”他说。 “他们希望看到年轻人参与其中，我到处都听到这样的说法。”
我可以相信民意调查吗？以及听众提出的有关 2026 年中期选举的其他问题
这位前州参议员和房地产开发商表示，他的平台可以与两党爱荷华州人对话。他呼吁限制众议院的任期，最多六届，并禁止国会股票交易。他说他还拒绝了企业政治行动委员会的竞选捐款。
这都是“反腐败平台”的一部分，他说这一焦点在他这一代人中是独一无二的，因为 30 岁以下的美国人表示高度关注自己的经济福祉和对机构的不信任。
“我只是认为年轻人——无论是两党还是无党派——都对这个制度感到沮丧，”他说。 “他们很沮丧，他们应该如此。”
目前，众议院只有一名议员属于 Z 世代：29 岁的佛罗里达州民主党人麦克斯韦·弗罗斯特 (Maxwell Frost)。然而，预计还有两名候选人将于周二获胜。 29 岁的民主社会主义者梅拉特·基罗斯有望赢得科罗拉多州第一选区，这是一个可靠的蓝色席位。 26 岁的共和党人迈克尔·阿方索 (Michael Alfonso) 预计将获得威斯康星州第七选区的席位，该选区是共和党占多数的席位。
阿方索是特朗普认可的政坛新人，他的丈夫是交通部长肖恩·达菲 (Sean Duffy) 的女儿。达菲曾于 2011 年至 2019 年担任该议员。如果当选，他将成为第一位在国会任职的 2000 年代出生的人。
在本月早些时候接受威斯康星州公共广播电台采访时，阿方索称自己的年龄是“最大的优势”。
威斯康星州第七国会选区美国众议院候选人迈克尔·阿方索 (Michael Alfonso) 于 2026 年 8 月 4 日在威斯康星州新里士满举行的竞选活动中与与会者握手。艾伦·施密特/美联社隐藏标题栏
“我和第七区的每个人都有相同的价值观，”阿方索说。 “努力工作、信仰和家庭。”
但在20多岁的年纪作为候选人参选并获胜在政坛仍然是罕见的。随着年龄最大的 Z 世代明年将年满 30 岁，这一代人才刚刚开始有资格在众议院任职，众议院的最低年龄为 25 岁。
根据支持年轻人当选公职的无党派组织“未来核心小组”的一份报告，本周期全国范围内的国会候选人中只有 4% 属于 Z 世代，这是所有一代中通过初选的可能性最小的一代。
此外，虽然作为年轻人竞选国会议员的情况仍然很少见，但作为年轻的共和党人竞选国会议员的情况就更少见了。
未来核心小组的数据显示，今年竞选国会的 Z 世代候选人中，大多数是民主党人，只有不到三分之一的人是共和党人。另外 16% 的人没有与任何一方交往或选择第三方。

title_en: An NFL team just won a game without completing a pass. No, seriously.
title_zh: 一支 NFL 球队在没有完成传球的情况下刚刚赢得了一场比赛。不，说真的。
summary: Facing the Atlanta Falcons in a game played amid a downpour, the Tampa By Buccaneers attempted only three passes. And won.
summary_zh: 在一场倾盆大雨中面对亚特兰大猎鹰队的比赛中，坦帕海盗队仅尝试了 3 次传球。并赢了。
body_en: An NFL team just won a game without completing a pass. No, seriously.
The offense run by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday was the most predictable of the 2026 NFL season.

Facing the Atlanta Falcons in a key divisional matchup of Week 8, in a game played in a downpour that left standing water pooling on the field in Raymond James Stadium, the Buccaneers attempted only three passes, completing none.
Unwilling and unable to throw in soggy conditions, they ran it 56 times. The strategy won them the game, 16-0.
“First time for everything,” Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles said.

To say it was an unusual game plan was an understatement. The last time an NFL team had more rushing attempts than Tampa’s 56 was in 2010. The Buccaneers were the first team to win without a completed pass since Buffalo in 1974, per the league . Rarer still was that a team hadn’t won by double digits without completing a pass since 1945, according to one NFL researcher .

The Buccaneers had been forced to rely on a ground-heavy offense last week, as well, when quarterback Baker Mayfield threw only 11 times in his first game back since he injured his thumb. Tampa rushed for 258 yards in that win against Carolina, then leaned on a similar plan Sunday as the forecast showed a storm rolling over Florida. Nearly an inch of rain had fallen over Tampa by kickoff, and the rain didn’t stop as the game began.
Mayfield finished 0-3 passing, but he was all smiles after the game, considering it was Tampa’s first home win this season after an 0-4 start.
Did Bowles tell Tampa Bay’s offensive coordinator not to pass?

“We didn’t say you’re not going to throw the ball; the conditions told him that,” Bowles said. “You could see it’s a downpour down there and the wind’s blowing. You can kind of see the ball’s not going anywhere.”

Against the Falcons, Tampa Bay gained a franchise-record 324 yards on the ground, an average of 5.8 yards per rush, as the backfield tandem of Bucky Irving (170 yards) and Kenny Gainwell (140) repeatedly ran through Atlanta’s defense.

Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix Jr. completed just eight of 24 passes and was intercepted four times and fumbled once. It was a marked difference from Penix’s last two games, in which he’d thrown for six touchdowns and zero interceptions combined. Mayfield fumbled three times, though he didn’t lose any. Irving did lose a fumble.
“It’s a win, so,” Mayfield said. “I’ll take it, man.”
Andrew Greif is a sports reporter for NBC News Digital.
body_zh: 一支 NFL 球队在没有完成传球的情况下刚刚赢得了一场比赛。不，说真的。
坦帕湾海盗队周日的进攻是 2026 年 NFL 赛季中最可预测的。
在第八周一场关键的分区对决中，海盗队面对亚特兰大猎鹰队，这场比赛是在倾盆大雨中进行的，雷蒙德·詹姆斯体育场的球场上积满了积水，海盗队只尝试了 3 次传球，没有成功。
由于不愿意也无法在潮湿的环境中进行投掷，他们跑了 56 次。 The strategy won them the game, 16-0.
“一切都是第一次，”海盗队教练托德·鲍尔斯说。
说这是一个不寻常的游戏计划是轻描淡写的。上一次 NFL 球队冲球次数超过坦帕队的 56 次是在 2010 年。根据联盟的数据，海盗队是自 1974 年布法罗队以来第一支在没有完成传球的情况下获胜的球队。一位 NFL 研究人员称，自 1945 年以来，更罕见的是，没有一支球队在没有完成传球的情况下以两位数获胜。
上周海盗队也被迫依靠地面进攻，四分卫贝克·梅菲尔德(Baker Mayfield)在拇指受伤后复出的第一场比赛中只投出了11次球。坦帕在战胜卡罗莱纳州的比赛中冲出了 258 码，然后在周日因天气预报显示佛罗里达州将有风暴而采取了类似的计划。开球时坦帕上空下了近一英寸的雨，比赛开始时雨并没有停止。
梅菲尔德完成了0-3的传球，但赛后他满脸笑容，考虑到这是坦帕在0-4开局后本赛季的首场主场胜利。
鲍尔斯是否告诉坦帕湾的进攻协调员不要传球？
“我们并没有说你不会扔球；条件告诉了他这一点，”鲍尔斯说。 “你可以看到下面正在下倾盆大雨，风在吹。你可以看到球不会去任何地方。”
在对阵猎鹰队的比赛中，坦帕湾队的冲球码数达到了队史纪录 324 码，平均每次冲球码数为 5.8 码，而巴基·欧文（170 码）和肯尼·甘威尔（140 码）的后场串联不断地冲破亚特兰大队的防线。
亚特兰大队四分卫小迈克尔·佩尼克斯 (Michael Penix Jr.) 24 次传球仅完成 8 次，并被拦截 4 次、掉球一次。这与佩尼克斯过去两场比赛有很大不同，在过去两场比赛中，他总共传球六次达阵，零次拦截。梅菲尔德失手三次，但没有失手。欧文确实失手了。
“这是一场胜利，所以，”梅菲尔德说。 “我会接受的，伙计。”
安德鲁·格雷夫 (Andrew Greif) 是 NBC 新闻数字频道的体育记者。

summary_zh: 宾夕法尼亚州州长乔什·夏皮罗 (Josh Shapiro) 周二以压倒性优势赢得连任，有望成为 2028 年总统候选人。新Y
body_en: Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro 's chances of being a presidential contender in 2028 are riding on his winning reelection in a landslide Tuesday.
New York Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez 's future hinges on whether a fellow progressive can carry a swing state, for once.

California Gov. Gavin Newsom has to show that his congressional redistricting gambit worked for Democrats — and he needs to beat back a state wealth tax proposal supported by Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.).

Driving the news: Democrats eyeing White House runs have spent the past year preparing to emerge from Tuesday's midterms with momentum, and an argument for a 2028 candidacy. They want Democrats to do well — but to each, some races are especially important.
Some have focused their time and money on particular contests for ideological reasons, or a desire to show strength in their home states.
Others have hedged their bets across the nation, so that Tuesday is unlikely to be a huge victory or a significant defeat.
Here's how the top potential Democratic contenders for president have placed their bets in this week's elections — and what success or failure will look like for them.

A great night: AOC has wagered just about everything on the Senate race in Michigan, where she's said that a win by progressive Abdul El-Sayed would "break open the entire political calculus in America" and show that "anybody can win anywhere."
She's weighing whether to run for president or the Senate, and much of her electability argument for a national campaign hinges on an El-Sayed victory.

Progressives are desperate to establish that one of their own can carry a presidential battleground state. Ocasio-Cortez has contributed $1 million to help El-Sayed and stumped for him at several events.

An El-Sayed victory "would prove to the country, and the world, that competent, courageous progressive populists can win in the most competitive swing states in America," said Bhavik Lathia, a left-wing strategist from Michigan.
"The implications for 2028 would be enormous."

AOC would get bonus points Tuesday if other progressives she's supporting — such as House candidate Randy Villegas in California and Senate candidate Angie Nixon in Florida — win their swing-seat races.
Worst-case scenario: If El-Sayed loses, many progressives think AOC would be less likely to run for president.
That's why she's widely viewed as having more on the line Tuesday than any other potential Democratic contender for president, followed by Shapiro.

A great night: Shapiro needs to win so big Tuesday that it makes Democratic presidential primary voters see his technocratic "get shit done" brand of governing as the party's best bet to take down the GOP in 2028.
Shapiro is less known nationally than many 2028 hopefuls, and that has been by choice. He's largely focused on Pennsylvania this year, even as would-be rivals for president crisscrossed the country.
A blowout in America's biggest swing state could help him stand out.

A good night for Shapiro would be defeating Republican Stacy Garrity by double digits and carrying three Democratic House candidates — Janelle Stelson, Bob Brooks and Paige Cognetti — across the finish line to defeat Republican incumbents.

He'd have a great night if his coattails were so long that he pulled a fourth Democratic House hopeful, Bob Harvie, to victory — taking down GOP Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick, who's known for surviving difficult electoral cycles.
body_zh: 宾夕法尼亚州州长乔什·夏皮罗 (Josh Shapiro) 周二以压倒性优势赢得连任，有望成为 2028 年总统候选人。
纽约州众议员亚历山大·奥卡西奥-科尔特斯的未来取决于这位进步人士是否能一次带领摇摆州。
加州州长加文·纽瑟姆必须证明他的国会重新划分选区策略对民主党有利，而且他需要驳回参议员伯尼·桑德斯（佛蒙特州）支持的州财富税提案。
推动这一消息的是：着眼于入主白宫的民主党人在过去的一年里一直在准备在周二的中期选举中势头强劲，并为 2028 年的候选资格展开辩论。他们希望民主党表现出色，但对每个人来说，有些种族都特别重要。
有些人出于意识形态原因，或者希望在自己的家乡展示实力，将时间和金钱集中在特定的比赛上。
其他人则在全国范围内对冲赌注，因此周二不太可能取得巨大胜利或重大失败。
以下是民主党总统候选人的最大潜在竞争者如何在本周的选举中下注，以及他们的成功或失败。
一个美好的夜晚：AOC 在密歇根州的参议院竞选中几乎下了所有赌注，她表示，进步派阿卜杜勒·赛义德的胜利将“打破美国的整个政治算计”，并表明“任何人都可以在任何地方获胜”。
她正在权衡是否竞选总统或参议院，而她在全国竞选中的当选论点很大程度上取决于埃尔赛义德的胜利。
进步人士迫切希望自己的人能够赢得总统的战场州。奥卡西奥-科尔特斯捐赠了 100 万美元来帮助埃尔-赛义德，并在多项活动中为他助阵。
来自密歇根州的左翼战略家巴维克·拉蒂亚 (Bhavik Lathia) 表示，埃尔赛义德的胜利“将向国家和世界证明，有能力、勇敢的进步民粹主义者能够在美国最具竞争力的摇摆州获胜”。
“这对 2028 年的影响将是巨大的。”
如果她支持的其他进步人士——例如加利福尼亚州的众议院候选人兰迪·维勒加斯和佛罗里达州的参议院候选人安吉·尼克松——赢得摇摆席位竞选，AOC 周二将获得加分。
最坏的情况：如果埃尔赛义德失败，许多进步人士认为 AOC 竞选总统的可能性较小。
这就是为什么人们普遍认为她周二比任何其他潜在的民主党总统候选人更有可能获胜，其次是夏皮罗。
一个美好的夜晚：夏皮罗周二需要赢得如此大的胜利，让民主党总统初选选民看到他的技术官僚“搞砸”的执政风格是该党在 2028 年推翻共和党的最佳选择。
夏皮罗在全国范围内的知名度不如许多 2028 年候选人，而这是他的选择。今年他主要关注宾夕法尼亚州，尽管潜在的总统竞争对手遍布全国。
在美国最大的摇摆州的井喷可能会帮助他脱颖而出。
对夏皮罗来说，一个美好的夜晚将以两位数的优势击败共和党人史黛西·加里蒂，并带领三名民主党众议院候选人——贾妮尔·斯特尔森、鲍勃·布鲁克斯和佩奇·科涅蒂——冲过终点线，击败共和党现任议员。
如果他的尾气足够长，能够拉动第四位民主党众议院候选人鲍勃·哈维(Bob Harvie)取得胜利，击败以在艰难的选举周期中幸存而闻名的共和党众议员布莱恩·菲茨帕特里克(Brian Fitzpatrick)，那么他将度过一个美好的夜晚。

OpenAI might rebrand its data centers as ‘AI compute campuses’
Data centers are deeply unpopular . But what if we called them something else?
Axios reports that OpenAI is preparing a “PR blitz” for after the midterm elections on Tuesday, as Democrats seem likely to win back the House of Representatives, and possibly the Senate, too .

The company’s chief global affairs officer Chris Lehane told Axios that the midterms will be “a bit of a movie trailer for what you’re going to see in 2028,” when he expects AI to be “ the issue” in the presidential election.

So OpenAI is to influence the AI debate moving forward, with Lehane discussing several proposals, including the development of AI “speed limits” ; finding ways to help people see AI as empowering them in their daily lives; pushing the U.S. to take a role in developing global standards — and yes, rebranding data centers as “AI compute campuses.”

Lehane also described the conversation around data centers (a debate that has pushed Amazon and Microsoft to say they will no longer use NDAs in their negotiations with local governments ) as “good and healthy.”
“Communities should hold companies responsible and accountable so they really and truly get a transformative benefit from these projects,” he said.
